cards.title: Text pipelines: per-use literal String allocation, owned split results and redundant clones
cards.body:
Generated Rust for line-oriented corpus entries (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json), 'jet emit --rust') shows general codegen costs on every line of input:

- string literal arguments allocate on each use ('" ".to_string()' three times per line in logreport; '"".to_string()' for an equality test)
- 'jet_unicode_split_once' returns owned (before, after) Strings, then the emitter '.clone()'s the fields again (14 clones in logreport's loop)
- every user function call pays 'jet_stack_enter(...)' plus a JetOutcome wrapper even when infallible (bump() per line)
- map lookups clone the key twice ('get(&key.clone()).cloned()')
- datasummary: group_by/sort_by_compare clone each record (8 clones), float ordering through a comparator host

Measured AOT losses: logreport 4.0x Rust, 4.2x Python, 7.1x Zig, 6.3x Node, 2.8x Go (109 ms vs 27 ms); text-script 1.23x Rust; datasummary 11.7x Rust; taskfile-cli 1.13x Rust (2026-09-01 partial run, before its AOT ICE). These are the text.report-cli, text.script, numerics.script, numerics.notebook, cli.app and formats.json-app cells.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Remove the general per-line costs from AOT text pipelines: literal `String` allocation on each use, owned split results that get cloned again, doubled map-key clones, cloned records in group_by/sort, and stack frames on infallible calls. Output bytes, diagnostics and tier behavior stay the same. This is one emitter and ownership path, not a fast path per corpus entry, and it adds no public API.

## Current state
- Measured AOT losses (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl): logreport 4.0x Rust (109 ms vs 27 ms), 4.2x Python, 7.1x Zig, 6.3x Node, 2.8x Go; text-script 1.23x Rust; datasummary 11.7x Rust; taskfile-cli 1.13x Rust. These are the text.report-cli, text.script, numerics.script, numerics.notebook, cli.app and formats.json-app cells.
- The Jet Rust printer turns every MIR String constant into an owned String: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:1344` (`.String(value) -> "{quote}.to_string()"`) and the const-key path at `:1389`.
- Split routes through `jet_unicode_split_once` with owned arguments: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet:522`. The Prelude already borrows its inputs: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/UnicodeString.rs:131` takes `(&str, &str)` and returns owned `(String, String)`.
- The shipped Rust printer already skips the stack frame for infallible functions in release. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:12064-12099` wraps `jet_stack_enter` in `#[cfg(not(jet_release))]` unless the function is fallible, unsafe or policy-scoped. The Jet printer (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Functions.jet:429`) emits only sentry and deadline scopes.
- The split-literal borrow fix from 2026-09-21 (ebe828003) exists only in the archived MIRRust.rs.

## Changes
1. Jet lowering (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/{Expressions,BuiltinMethods,Statements,Functions}.jet`): when the checked ownership and escape facts prove a value does not escape, pass literal arguments, split results, map keys and group_by/sort records as borrowed MIR operands (`MirAccess.Read` place or const). Values that escape stay owned.
2. Jet printer (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/{Types,Operations,Values}.jet`):
   - Print a borrowed String constant as a `&str` literal where the Prelude parameter is `&str`.
   - Stop re-cloning split-result fields.
   - Print map `get` with one borrowed key.
   - Port the ebe828003 split-literal rule.
3. Jet printer (`Emit/Functions.jet`): match the MIRRust.rs:12065 rule. The default profile gets no frame for `MirFailureCarrier.Infallible` functions without unsafe or policy scopes. Debug and hardened profiles keep the frame.
4. Rust mirror, so the shipped binary proves the change: apply the same borrow rules in `MIRRust.rs`. Change Prelude signatures in `Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Text.rs` and `Prelude/Core/Collections.rs` only where the checked ABI already allows a borrow. Add no second text representation.
5. Add a witness `line_parsing_witness_borrows_literals_and_split_results` in `tests/tir_collections_and_methods.rs`. It covers literal args, split_once, map lookup, group_by and sort. It asserts on the emitted Rust and calls `assert_tiers_agree`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods -- line_parsing_witness`: passes. The loop body has no `" ".to_string()`, no `.clone()` of split fields, and no `get(&key.clone())`. O0, O1 and O2 output are identical.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=strings/ ...`: no golden changes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: no new errors in the touched JetCodegen files compared with the pre-change receipt.
- Measurement (batch-measure pass): run `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry X` for logreport, text-script, datasummary and taskfile-cli. Jet/peer must be < 1.00 for every peer, Rust included, on every metric, and Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 against the asm-parity reference. Record each loss separately.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: this is Jet lowering and printer work, with the MIRRust.rs mirror landing in the same build.

## Dependencies
None blocking. The ownership facts are already checked by sema.

AsmPar-1 measured logreport on dev bb770de593 + AsmPar-38..42: 3,720M → 2,976M instructions; w10 370.6M → 252.9M.
- The remaining allocator cost is structural: 6 rt_text_slice copies per line (split_once ×3, 2 parts each). Each copy is a 24-byte header plus a separate data buffer, so 12 allocs and 12 frees per line, about 800 of the ~9.9k instructions per line.
- Removing it needs a text representation change: either inline small text, with header and data in one block (15+ runtime files read text +16 and its cap directly), or borrowed text views as on this card.
- Deferred past the 2026-11-01 deadline.

AsmPar-1, 2026-11-01: split_once views were parked. A view header with cap 0 reads as an immortal literal, so jet_rt_string_clone returns the same pointer and a clone of a view would alias a dead frame. logreport hands the halves straight to user calls that clone them (bump does counts[key] =), and at IR build time nothing proves a callee never clones, so a conservative rule declines every use. A sound design needs either an interprocedural 'param never owned' fact or a runtime borrowed-header class that clone copies. In the post-fix logreport profile, split_once costs 15.7% (2 rt_text_copy plus 2 alloc/free per call, 3 calls per line).

cards.title: HTTP substrate after #2255: http-service p50 3.2x Go, concurrency-service loses to Node, http-client 1.25x Rust, run-tier probes time out
cards.body:
Fresh matched cells on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) for the shared HTTP serving and client substrate:

- http-service (netserv.service) AOT p50: Jet/Go 3.19x, Jet/Node 1.90x, Jet/Rust 1.58x, Jet/Python 1.09x; p99: Jet/Go 92.9x, Jet/Node 1.38x, Jet/Rust 1.24x. Run and dev tiers failed probe 2 (PUT /kv) with an HTTP probe timeout while the AOT tier passed every probe.
- concurrency-service (concurrency.service) AOT p50: 8.5 ms vs Node 8.05 ms (1.06x); wins Go 0.93x, Rust 0.94x, Python 0.90x. Startup on run/dev: 1.03-1.10x Go and Node.
- http-client (netserv.client) AOT wall: 1.25x Rust; wins Go 0.63x, Python 0.04x, Node 0.02x.

#2255 closed on its implementation evidence; these are the cells that remain red.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Turn the remaining red HTTP-substrate cells green after #2255, and first fix the run/dev-tier probe hang (I9).

**Measured baseline** (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl, release compiler)
- http-service (netserv.service) AOT:
  - p50: Jet/Go 3.19x, Jet/Node 1.90x, Jet/Rust 1.58x, Jet/Python 1.09x.
  - p99: Jet/Go 92.9x, Jet/Node 1.38x, Jet/Rust 1.24x.
  - The run and dev tiers fail probe 2 (PUT /kv) with an HTTP probe timeout. AOT passes every probe.
- concurrency-service AOT:
  - p50 8.5 ms vs Node 8.05 ms (1.06x). It wins against Go 0.93x, Rust 0.94x and Python 0.90x.
  - Startup on run/dev is 1.03-1.10x Go and Node.
- http-client AOT wall: 1.25x Rust. It wins against Go 0.63x, Python 0.04x and Node 0.02x.
- Targets: Jet/{Rust,Go,Node,Python} < 1.00 on every listed cell and tier, and Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 against the asm-parity reference.

**Current state**
- Server: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/{HTTPServer.rs,HTTPMessage.rs,HTTPRoute.rs}`. Client: `HTTPClient.rs`, `NetHTTP.rs`. `Core/http/server.jet` delegates to the native provider.
- JIT marshalling: `crates/jet-jit/src/{net_http_rt.rs,net_http_hosts.rs,Net.rs}`.
- Tests: `tests/http_i9.rs`, `tests/http_server_lifecycle.rs`, `tests/http.rs`, `tests/services_runtime.rs`.
- Gauntlet: `Tools/gauntlet/entries/{http-service,concurrency-service,http-client}` (`jet/run.jet`, `entry.json` probes). The harness is `Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry <name>`.

**Changes (in order)**
1. I9 first:
   - Reproduce with `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Tools/gauntlet/entries/http-service/jet/run.jet` plus the entry.json probes. The second probe never answers.
   - Trace where the JIT-tier server blocks: a blocking accept-loop read, or a task that never yields while a Shared write is pending.
   - Fix it in marshalling only, so the JIT host hands requests to the same scheduler path AOT uses.
   - Add `kv_get_put_get_matches_across_tiers` to `tests/http_i9.rs`.
2. Attribute on the current tree with `perf record` on the AOT binary under harness load: health vs kv, Shared state on/off, prebuilt vs formatted response, accept wakeups, per-request allocations. Record the split on the card.
3. Server substrate (HTTPServer/HTTPMessage/HTTPRoute): headers prebuilt once per route, no per-request `String` for static parts, one `writev` per response, keep-alive without a wakeup per request, a bounded accept batch.
4. Client (HTTPClient/NetHTTP): connection reuse and one allocation per response body.
- Writable paths: the Prelude files above, the jet-jit net files (marshalling only), and `tests/http_i9.rs`.
- Do not touch: `Tools/gauntlet/entries/` sources, `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs`, `crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs`, or `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs`.
- Non-goals: HTTP API, authority model, TLS, and scheduler policy in a host.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases http_i9/ --test http_server_lifecycle --test http --test services_runtime` → green.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry http-service`, then `--entry concurrency-service`, then `--entry http-client` → every probe passes on AOT, run and dev with identical responses, and the ratios meet criteria 1-3. Any losing cell stays on the card.

**Batch**
batch-host-runtime: Prelude HTTP runtime, JIT host marshalling, and tier parity.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: #Layout(columnar) particles run 15x slower than AoS and lose the packed arithmetic AoS gets
cards.body:
Actual: the same N=2,000 particle update (x += vx*dt, y += vy*dt, checksum of mass*(x+y)) built three ways. AoS `List<Particle>`: AOT median 0.0126 s, disassembly has `vmulpd 15 / vaddpd 5 / vsubpd 5`. Manual SoA (five lists): 0.0118 s. Ratified columnar `#Layout(c)` (D-SOA1/2): 0.180 s in both dev and release, and its packed list has zero arithmetic mnemonics (moves and masks only). All three print `599.9999999999977`. Generated Rust for columnar goes through `JetColumnList<...>::from_aos(vec![])` and per-field `.cell(k, i)` accessors (`s5_columnar.rs:71530-71557`); AoS goes through `Vec<__jet_Particle>` field loads (`s5_aos.rs:71456-71473`).

Expected: the layout ratified to make SIMD-shaped work vectorize must be at least as fast as AoS on the shape it exists for, and must expose contiguous column slices that LLVM vectorizes. A 15x regression on the ratified path violates the performance budget law (docs/spec/performance-budget-decisions.md) on its own headline case.

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/simd/results.md S5; sources s5_*.jet; generated Rust s5_aos.rs, s5_columnar.rs; hyperfine JSON and objdump dumps in the lane directory.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make the ratified columnar layout (`#Layout(c)`, D-SOA1/D-SOA2) at least as fast as AoS on the particle update it exists for, and vectorize it the same way.

Measured, N=2,000 (`x += vx*dt`, `y += vy*dt`, checksum of `mass*(x+y)`):

| Layout | AOT median | Particle-loop arithmetic |
|---|---|---|
| AoS `List<Particle>` | 0.0126 s | `vmulpd` 15 / `vaddpd` 5 / `vsubpd` 5 |
| Manual SoA | 0.0118 s | — |
| Columnar | 0.180 s (dev and release) | none, only moves and masks |

All three print `599.9999999999977`. The 15x loss breaks the performance-budget law (`Docs/spec/performance-budget-decisions.md`) on the layout's headline case. Evidence: `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/simd/results.md` S5.

## Current state
- Jet printer: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:1578-1597` `jet_rust_emit_columnar_read` prints every read as `(base).cell(k, i, file, line).jet_col_<field>()`. That is a per-element enum match with no loop-invariant typed projection.
- Lowering goes through `jet_columns_gather_cell` (`Codegen/Expressions.jet:4729-4733`, `MirSemanticOp.ColumnarRead`). Legality facts are at `Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Verification/Legality.jet:721-723`.
- `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Evaluator.jet:7662,8347` reads per element through a Prelude argument vector.
- Host code:
  - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Columns.rs` `gather`/`gather_cell` build `views()` on every call.
  - `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/Collections.rs` rebuilds `JetColumns::from_rows` on every read.
- The witness exists: `tests/s5_columnar_witness.rs` with `tests/s5_columnar_witness/{aos,columnar}.jet`. It checks output identity only.
- The dependency cards are all done: #2888, #2892, #2895, #2899 and #2893. #2893 owns automatic AoS→SoA transposition, which is out of scope here.

## Changes
1. Optimizer (`Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Facts/LoopVector.jet`, `Verification/Legality.jet`): for a read-only numeric columnar scan whose field is loop-invariant, record a typed column projection. That is one typed field slice per touched field, hoisted before the loop. Log it in the #2899 decision ledger with its one-time cost.
2. Jet printer (`jet_rust_emit_columnar_read`):
   - When the fact is present, print plain indexed reads on a borrowed `&[f64]` (or the proven field type), keeping the shared bounds check and the error location.
   - Otherwise, keep today's route.
   - Mirror the same printing in the shipped MIRRust.rs.
3. JetEval: add direct column access with no per-element argument vector.
4. Host:
   - `Columns.rs`: `gather`/`gather_cell` use stable column borrows and stop allocating `views()`.
   - JIT: keep the column store for the whole operation.
   - Row views, serialization and whole-record gather stay unchanged.
5. Extend `tests/s5_columnar_witness.rs` with `s5_columnar_release_loop_is_packed`, which checks the release binary's `objdump` for `vmulpd`/`vaddpd` in the particle loop.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases s5_columnar_witness/`: both tests pass. Output is identical on O0, O1 and O2, and the columnar loop has packed f64 instructions.
- Measurement: build `tests/s5_columnar_witness/{aos,columnar}.jet` with `jet build --release`, then run `hyperfine -w 3 -r 20 ./aos ./columnar`. The columnar median must be ≤ the AoS median.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: optimizer fact and printer, with the host Columns and JIT fixes in the same build.

## Dependencies
None. All the prerequisite cards are done.
cards.checkSteps:
Planned proof only; not run during preparation. Rebuild before compiler/runtime smoke. Run repository commands through scripts/agent/jet-env. Use exact narrow criterion evidence; broad suites remain milestone-gated.

Use the same S5 fixtures and same machine; every Jet invocation goes through `scripts/agent/jet-env`.

1. Build both fixtures in release and run the packet's existing hyperfine comparison. Observable result: columnar median is <= AoS median under the existing strict gate; report raw runs, candidate identity, CPU, and output.
2. Inspect the generated release artifact and run `objdump -d` over the particle loop. Observable result: `vmulpd` and `vaddpd` occur in the columnar loop, and the loop body has no `jet_columns_gather_cell`, `views()`, or per-element generated cell-enum field match. A source inspection of generated Rust must show one typed projection before the loop, not a `Vec`/projection recreated inside it.
3. Run the three variants through release AOT, `scripts/agent/jet-env jet run`, and `scripts/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret`. Observable result: each prints `599.9999999999977`.
4. Run negative/edge cells: empty columnar list, zero-field record, out-of-range positive/negative index, mixed field widths if representable, and whole-record serialization. Observable result: errors and row/field order match the pre-change canonical operation; no typed projection bypasses bounds or changes serialization.
5. Run the JIT and interpreter parity rows from the card. Observable result required by the existing card is output parity; the implementation proof additionally records that JIT does not rebuild from rows per read and interpreter does not allocate a per-element prelude argument vector.

cards.title: Declare catalog-free release inputs for existing binary recipes
cards.body: Define a catalog-free, self-authored release declaration for the `Releases` source (`RefSource.Releases`). D-RELEASE-RECIPE1 compares A, fields beside source, with B, Recipe.release around exactly one existing installer. Both are proposed surfaces, not shipped APIs. Direct GitHub and HTTPS feeds use D-RELEASE-TRUST1, automatic observed-byte hashes, and no public feed signature or key protocol.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship the ratified D-RELEASE-RECIPE1=A declaration: `Pkg.adapt` carries `resolver:` and `asset:` beside `source:` for the `Releases` source (`RefSource.Releases`), around exactly one existing installer. Option B (`Recipe.release`) is rejected and must not exist.

## Current state
- `Jetpack/EnvModel/Source/ModuleEval/PackageSugar.jet:79-96` `envmodel_parse_adapter` admits only `name`, `source`, `deps`, `recipe` (`:81` field list); every shape error is E1270 (`:299-300`).
- Field spellings live in `Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Syntax.jet:403-409` (`@ADAPTER_FIELD_*`, `@RECIPE_*`).
- The `Releases` source (`RefSource.Releases`) exists only as a ref source: `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Refs/RefSpec.jet:45,66,110`, mapped to `ProviderKind.JetPackage` in `Jetpack/EnvModel/Source/ModuleEval/SourceLoader.jet:304`.
- No `ReleaseResolver`, `ReleaseAssetSelector` or `Sha256` type exists anywhere in `Jetpack/`.
- PackageSugar.jet has uncommitted edits from another writer: coordinate before you edit it.

## Changes
1. `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Release/ReleaseModel.jet` (new, listed in `Jetpack/Bootstrap/sources.list`): the finite family `ReleaseResolver` (`Release.github`, `Release.https{metadata, origins, decoder}`), `ReleaseFeed`, `ReleaseCandidate`, `ReleaseAsset`, `ReleaseAssetSelector`, `ReleaseAssetKind`, `ReleaseFormat`, `ReleaseEntryMode`, `Sha256`, `ReleaseDecodeError`. The pure decoder contract has no signature, key or proof field.
2. Same module, pure validation used later by the Provider seam: nonempty fields, RFC3339 times, HTTPS-only URLs, safe relative root and entry, size and extraction bounds, and `sha256_parse` (bare 64-hex or `sha256:<64-hex>` → lowercase; whitespace, wrong length, non-hex and unknown algorithms fail; None stays None). Add `release_origin_admits(scope, url)` so metadata, artifact and redirect origins are checked before any request; the scope cannot be widened after the fact.
3. `Syntax.jet` and the syntax registry (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax`): add `@ADAPTER_FIELD_RESOLVER`, `@ADAPTER_FIELD_ASSET` and the `Release.*` spellings.
4. `PackageSugar.jet` `envmodel_parse_adapter`: accept `resolver:` and `asset:` only when the source classifies as `RefSource.Releases`, with exactly one Copy, Prebuilt or Build recipe. Reject release fields on other sources, duplicate selector fields, a second fetch and any `Recipe.release` spelling with E1270, and extend the E1270 help text. `Release.github` takes no repository argument; it derives owner/repo from the source.
5. Record the ratified surface in `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` and the packaging spec (A only; B absent).
Provider wiring, trust and staging belong to #3031, #3032 and #3033. `BuildStep.fetch` hash and credential-free laws do not change.

## Proof
- `JETPACK_WORKER=rel Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area EnvModel --tests` prints `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`. It runs new claims in `Jetpack/PackageModel/Tests/Release.jet` (SHA-256 table, RFC3339/URL/path/size rejections, origin admission) and `Jetpack/EnvModel/Tests/ModuleEvalReleases.jet` (the complete Acme HTTPS example with three ordered origins and one archive selector is accepted; release fields on a non-Releases source, a duplicate `asset:` and `Recipe.release(...)` each give E1270).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env target/debug/jet self devtools grammars` produces no diff, because these are field names, not lexer tokens. That satisfies criteria 13-14 without re-blessing.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-envmodel: the EnvModel area unit (with its PackageModel closure) proves the whole declaration.

## Dependencies
None open.

cards.title: Preserve checked loop and access proofs from sema facts into JetIR
cards.body: The checked TIR carries AutoVectorizationFacts on Range/CountedLoop, but tir_to_mir_stmt.rs discards the Range payload as auto_vectorization: _ and the current MIR loop lowering does not retain its provenance. The canonical optimizer then derives vector facts using CFG/operation/root heuristics. Carry the checked semantic evidence into the existing MIR fact mechanism so all adapters consume the same scoped proof. Root-string aliasing is a provenance risk; no legal alias miscompile has been demonstrated.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Carry the checked AutoVectorizationFacts from TIR into the existing MIR fact channel, bound to stable loop, value and access IDs with origin and validity window. Every adapter then consumes one scoped semantic proof instead of re-deriving eligibility from CFG and root-name heuristics.

## Current state
- Partly ported. Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Statements.jet:570-595 jet_codegen_record_checked_vector_fact records a MirVectorFact with accesses `[]` and a hard-coded Rejected(UnsupportedOperation) decision. Loop lowerings pass the facts in (:597,632,672,966).
- Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:320-322 and Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Statements.jet:183 carry the facts.
- Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Facts/LoopVector.jet:33-79 re-derives structural facts.
- Earlier Rust work (fca9168a2) honored Reduction/ConditionalAccumulate/EarlyExitSearch semantics in the archived optimizer and is reference only.

## Changes
1. Statements.jet jet_codegen_record_checked_vector_fact: bind facts to the MIR loop header, cursor, body blocks and each access (place ID and operation ID), with source span origin and a validity window (the block set). The decision comes from the checked facts, not a constant.
2. JetFoundation MIR: extend MirVectorFact/checked_vector_facts in place, with no parallel schema. Update canonical serialization and digest.
3. LoopVector.jet: reconcile structural CFG facts with the carried proof. A structural fact never overrides a semantic rejection, and a missing alias/effect/order proof stays a rejection, never a root-name guess. Transforms (FixedReduction and the others) invalidate or rebind facts whose subject they change.
4. Verification/Legality.jet and every consumer (Emit, JetEval, the retained Cranelift host) read the canonical fact. #Scalar, early exits, effects and cross-iteration dependence stay conservative; exact reduction bits are preserved.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- Goldens and the harness row per add_criteria.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: codegen fact recording plus optimizer reconciliation. #3040 and #3447 build on it in the same batch.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: One checked fact owner for developer tools: hover, signature help, calls and inspect show the same callable contract (D-ONE-TOOLS1=A)
cards.body:
Show the checked callable contract at ambient and foreign boundaries.

A reader needs the callable's actual arity, parameter/result identity, failure and rights facts. A declaration stub may omit behavior handled by a special semantic path.

First compare print hover/signature help, qualified calls and the checked callable record. If they disagree, make existing presentation consume the authoritative checked contract. Keep unknown external behavior distinct from checked Jet guarantees; do not infer effect facts from return-type dispatch tables.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-big-f04. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Ownership reconciliation: Exact #2986 owns named Core module drift and generated declaration/dispatch conformance; its current plan does not own ambient print hover/signature agreement. This new bounded presentation proof coordinates with that producer rather than adding hidden work to its criterion.

Exact final evidence boundary: Declaration and special semantic arm differ in expressed arity. No hover mismatch or terminal-effect propagation failure is observed.

Owner choice: None for agreement with the existing checked contract. No new effect syntax or analysis safety exemption is proposed.
cards.plan:
## Goal
One checked fact owner for developer tools (D-ONE-TOOLS1=A). Calls, hover, signature help, diagnostics and reasoning views show the same checked callable contract (arity, parameter/result identity, failure and rights facts) at ambient and foreign boundaries, with no parallel analyzer.

## Current state
- The Jet fact owner exists. `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/CompilerQueries.jet:10-13` defines `JetDriverCompilerCheckResult{checked: JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts?, diagnostics, failed_stage}`, and `Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet:39-42,399` builds `JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts{value, semantic_index_complete}`.
- The host tools still run their own projections. The LSP has a private `CheckedBundle` (`Source/LSP/Server.rs:51-54`: diags, `ProgramBundle`, `SemIndexEffectFacts`). `jet inspect` has `CheckProjection` (`Source/CmdInspect.rs:35-38`: bundle, facts, `jet_semindex::SemIndex`). Both are built from the archived Rust sema/semindex.
- Recorded evidence boundary: the `print` declaration stub and its special semantic arm disagree on arity. No hover mismatch has been observed yet.
- Coverage today: `tests/lsp.rs` has `lsp_hover_returns_signature` (:3055) and `lsp_signature_help_returns_active_parameter` (:2480).

## Changes
1. Step 1, now, host only: add the print hover/signature/call comparison test. Where the declaration and the semantic arm disagree, make the presentation read the checked callable record. Do not infer effects from return-type tables. Keep unknown foreign behaviour marked unknown.
2. Step 2, after #218 routes execute: define one typed projection of `JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts` that carries source, overlay, target, settings and package identity across the host boundary (`Compiler/Bootstrap/Host`). Replace `CheckedBundle` and `CheckProjection` with consumers of that projection in `Source/LSP/{Server,Check,Features}.rs` and `Source/CmdInspect.rs`, and delete the Rust-side analyzers in the same cutover.
3. Derive compiler CLI flag ownership from the command declarations. App `ArgsSpec` (#3242) keeps its own schema.
4. Preserve registered codes, fixes, byte/UTF-16 spans, URI escaping, privacy and every LSP, report and replay contract. A backend failure stays an internal error (I2).

## Proof
- The added criterion (print parity test).
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases lsp/` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases live_inspect/` stay green after the cutover.
- A pure-looking helper that adds an outward operation shows the updated rights/failure explanation in hover and in `jet inspect --json` output (criterion 3).

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: the LSP and inspect consumers are host CLI/tooling.

## Dependencies
Step 2 needs #218 (the Jet check query must execute through the host). #3325 owns operation facts, which this card consumes. #2986 owns Core module drift.

3. A pure-looking helper that adds an outward operation updates the relevant rights/failure explanation or produces the applicable registered diagnostic; exact behavior requires a runtime/front-end probe.
4. Foreign/generated origins and unknown analysis boundaries are visible without asking the reader to inspect compiler special cases.

cards.title: One Codable contract: options, field metadata, enum shapes, override precedence, schema and losslessness
cards.body:
Destination: generated and hand-written codecs share one typed contract (D-ONE-CODECS1=A): one owner for field traversal, override precedence and field-error paths, decode returning [FieldError] (D-VALIDATE-DECODE1=B), the D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1=A marker forms only, and each wire format keeping its own leaves (duplicate keys, binary or text, extension tags, mixed XML, lossless numbers).

Why it matters: codecs are every program's boundary; two traversals or two marker vocabularies mean two answers for the same type.

Current code: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet (admissibility, wire reachability); Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/AutoDerives.jet and EncodingCodecs.jet (generation).

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md (finding core-f007), compared with selected Serde, Glaze and Jackson mappings without importing their reflection systems.

Ballot: the spelling of adjacent tagging, retained unknown variants and decode aliases under D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1 is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close custom-codec and reflection interoperability under D-ONE-CODECS1=A, with D-VALIDATE-DECODE1=B stated as current law. Field traversal, constraint application, override precedence and field-error paths get one canonical owner. Each wire format keeps its own leaves (duplicate keys, binary/text, extension tags, mixed XML, lossless numerics). The comparison targets are selected Serde, Glaze and Jackson custom mappings, without importing their reflection systems. No new marker, public error family, data-algebra category or storage mechanism is added.

## Current state
- The original finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f007`. The old `docs/` path is stale.
- Sema: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet` checks codec admissibility, generic bounds and wire reachability (`sema_serde_field_reaches_wire` at :94, `sema_serde_type_is_admissible` at :148). Registration lives at `Registration/Checked.jet:140-141`.
- Codegen: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:277-286` lowers type-level `MirSerdeAttribute` (RenameAll, Tag, Untagged, DenyUnknownFields). `AutoDerives.jet` and `EncodingCodecs.jet` generate Encode/Decode.
- The format adapters are `Core/encoding/*.jet` and the host kernel `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/JSONCodec.rs`.
- Existing witnesses in `Examples/features/serde/`: `hand_codec`, `field_metadata_edges`, `serde_derive`, `serde_generic`, `codable_default`, `decode_migration`, `json_typed`, `csv_typed`, `cbor_profile`, plus the `encoding_*_stream` examples.

## Changes
1. Capability inventory (criteria 1 and 3). Build a table covering alias, rename, skip, read-only, constraints, variants, enums, chrono, custom context and generic targets. For each row give the Jet spelling (derived and hand-written), the owning code (Serde.jet / AutoDerives.jet / EncodingCodecs.jet / Core adapter) and the status: supported, missing-by-law or missing-defect. Classify every missing capability before proposing anything. A new marker or API needs its own ballot. The table goes in the card log.
2. One owner (criterion 4). Move field traversal, constraint application and error-path construction into one helper set in `AutoDerives.jet`, which `EncodingCodecs.jet` and every format adapter call. The precedence rule is: an explicit custom codec wins, then field attributes, then type-level `MirSerdeAttribute`, then derived defaults. Format syntax errors stay distinct from field errors.
3. Formats (criterion 5): full, selective and streaming decoding must agree in meaning for each profile. Streaming does not fake buffering or allocation parity.
4. Add examples for any gaps the inventory finds: `Examples/features/serde/codec_override_precedence.jet` and `codec_field_errors.jet`, each with a golden.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden serde/`: passes on O0, O1 and O2, including the two new examples.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases auto_derive_policy/`: passes.
- The capability table (criteria 1 and 3) is attached to the card log.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: the consolidation lives in derive generation (AutoDerives and EncodingCodecs). The Core adapters ride in the same build.

## Dependencies
None. D-ONE-CODECS1 is ratified.

questions.text: what is the most common way to handle this? what is the industry preference/best practice?
questions.answer: You asked what is most common and what the best practice is. Library defaults split. Swift's synthesized Codable, Protocol Buffers' JSON form and JavaScript's JSON.stringify leave an absent optional out. Rust serde, Go encoding/json, Java Jackson and .NET System.Text.Json write null by default. (Sources and the full survey: ballot D-SERDE-ABSENT-OPTIONAL1, detail paragraphs Industry writers, Their switches, Industry readers.)

cards.title: One checked CLI model: #CLI and ArgsSpec share one Core parser, and the four CLI reference formats are generated from it
cards.body: One active implementation home for the ratified Markdown, man, ReST and YAML command-document outputs. Former cards #3291,#3292,#3293 become historical redirects. Every original criterion and immutable decision remains traceable; no output implementation is claimed complete.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Deliver the four ratified ArgsSpec reference projections from one checked command model: `to_markdown` (D-CORE-CLI-MARKDOWN1=A), `to_man` (D-CORE-CLI-MAN1=A), `to_rest` (D-CORE-CLI-REST1=A) and `to_yaml` (D-CORE-CLI-YAML1=A, exact version1 fields).

**Current state (dev 9a82866572)**
- No `to_markdown`, `to_man`, `to_rest` or `to_yaml` exists for ArgsSpec.
- ArgsSpec methods are typed in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/ProcessHandles.jet` (the op, arity, return and parameter tables), and `Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildExpr.jet` routes each one to its Core/Args/Args.jet function.

**Changes**
1. Add the ops `ArgsSpecToMarkdown`, `ToMan`, `ToRest` and `ToYaml` in ProcessHandles.jet. Each takes no arguments except `to_man(date: String)`, whose date is explicit, never ambient. Each returns `String` and has receiver access `Read`. Route them in BuildExpr.jet.
2. In Core/Args/Args.jet, add one command-doc projection (command path, inherited options, defaults, visibility and examples, with hidden and secret entries omitted) and four small renderers:
   - Markdown fences and anchors;
   - roff escaping with an explicit `.TH` date;
   - ReST sections and links;
   - YAML, through the Core YAML writer's escaping.
   Help text is never parsed.
3. Output is capped. Overflow and malformed metadata return the fallible error path, never a panic or exit.

**Proof**
The golden Examples/features/cli/args_reference.jet uses one fixture with nested, inherited, hidden and secret options, multiline punctuation and fences. It matches args_reference.out on O0, O1 and O2. A Jet consumer test runs `man -l` or `groff -man -Tutf8`, a YAML reader, `rst2html --halt=warning` and `pandoc -f gfm` on the output, and a missing consumer is SKIP-HOST.

**Dependencies**
None; all four decisions are ratified. Completion (#3241) and menus (#3294) stay separate.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Command names/options/examples/defaults agree with parsing and help.
2. deterministic output and escaping.
3. malformed/foreign embedded metadata fails safely.
4. source program is not executed to extract docs.
5. Compare the complete shared command fixture with parse/help and generated Markdown.
6. Exercise punctuation/fences/multiline text, descendant anchors and hidden/secret omission.
7. Verify real Markdown rendering plus bounded deterministic output.
8. Keep one schema/formatter owner and no target or filesystem side effects.

cards.title: Iterator selection and grouping: filter_map by carrier, map_while, find_map, scan, extrema, chunk_by, unique and dedup, and seeded shuffle
cards.body:
Destination: one-source iterator adapters with exact contracts: filter_map lets the callback carrier decide selection (absence skips, errors are never silently dropped), map_while and find_map exist, scan keeps state apart from output, extrema take explicit comparators, chunk_by and unique/dedup state their grouping laws, and shuffling and sampling go through one explicit seeded random state.

Why it matters: today filter_map drops errors from a Result callback, and the free shuffle hides its random state.

Decisions: D-ITER-SELECTION1, SCAN1, CMPSELECT1, KEYRUNS1, UNIQUE1, RNG1 (all A), D-RANDOMDIST1=A.

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f015.

Moved out 2026-11-15: multi-source and combinatoric adapters to the lazy multi-source adapters card.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-SELECTION1=A (ratified): lift the existing `filter_map` so that the callback carrier decides the selection rule.
- `-> U?` skips `None`.
- An explicitly returned `Result` keeps the ratified success-only selector.
- A callback failure effect propagates and is never silently dropped.

Add `map_while` (`None` stops) and `find_map` (`None` continues) under their own exact contracts; the triggering item is consumed. There is no new absence or error type and no second selector engine.

## Current state
- Jet typing already unwraps an `Option` success (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:607-614`) and routes to `TClosureOp.FilterMap` (`:864`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ClosureMethods.jet:65-67`).
- The runtime requires `Result`: `jet_iter_filter_map` needs `F: FnMut(&T) -> Result<U, E>` and calls `.ok()` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:2261-2268`, list form `:2551-2558`). As a result an `Option` callback cannot lower, and a propagating error is dropped.
- JIT: `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:11884` (`checked_iter_filter_map_typed`).
- `map_while` and `find_map` exist nowhere in `Collections.jet`.
- The only example is `Examples/features/collections/filter_map.jet` (Result form, successful parses).
- Merged from #3357: an error item survives an ordinary data-preserving map unless a selector explicitly drops it. Nested optional/outcome items, all-error sources and empty sources keep their types. Remainder behaviour follows #3331.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - `Collections.jet` records the callback carrier (Option vs Result vs failure effect) in the operation, and adds `map_while` and `find_map` rows (arity, argument type, result `Iter<U>` and `U?`).
   - Add `TClosureOp.MapWhile` and `.FindMap` in `TIR.jet`.
   - Add route rows in `ClosureMethods.jet`.
2. Host mirror for the shipped proof:
   - `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` tables.
   - `crates/jet-codegen/src/TIR/lower/builtins.rs` and `TIR/routes.rs`.
   - Prelude `Collections.rs`: an `Option` variant of `jet_iter_filter_map`, the Result variant kept, the failure route propagated, plus `jet_iter_map_while` and `jet_iter_find_map`.
   - `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs`.
   - Interpreter `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs`.
3. Docs: the iterator family list in `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:308-312`.

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/collections/filter_map_absence.jet` prints `[1,3]` for `odd` (`-> Int?`) and keeps successful parses via Result. It also shows a propagated callback failure, error-as-data (#3357), `map_while` stopping at the first `None` with the remainder observable, and `find_map` skipping `None`.
  - `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/filter_map Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` covers both examples.
  - `JET_1216_STEM=collections/filter_map_absence Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`. This is a lazy-adapter runtime change proved by three-tier goldens; it batches with #3328/#3349/#3377/#3384/#3317.

## Dependencies
None. #3331 defines remainder semantics; coordinate with it, it does not block.

2. A propagating callback error, deliberate successful-item selection and error-as-data are distinct observed contracts.
3. Map-until-absence and first-success search retain their source remainder and terminating-item rules.

cards.title: One explicit destination protocol: FromIterator, extend, partition, sum and typed collection heads
cards.body:
Destination: FromIterator is the one user-extensible way to build a collection from a source (D-ITER-COLLECT1=A); the destination is always explicit at the call; collect and to_list stay List terminals; typed collection heads take a loop (D-COMPREHEND1=A); extend, partition and the aggregates use the same protocol.

Why it matters: without one protocol each collection grows its own constructor, and an expected type that silently changes a loop's result breaks reasoning about cost and order.

State (dev 168e1e9e92): no FromIterator trait; collect and to_list return List; Set.from takes a List.

Decisions: D-ITER-COLLECT1=A, D-COMPREHEND1=A, D-ITER-EXTEND1=A, D-ITER-BRANCHPARTITION1=A, D-COMPREHENSION1=A.

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md (finding iter-f017). Mapping owned items moved to #6871 c7.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-COLLECT1=A. `FromIterator` becomes the one user-extensible destination-construction protocol: one `Item` type, and `from(source)` consumes the source through the canonical Iterable conversion. The existing `Set.from` adopts it. List, Map, text, tuple and custom destinations own their ordering, duplicate and failure-cleanup policies. `collect()` and `to_list()` stay List terminals, and an expected type never changes eager or yielding behaviour. Extending existing state stays with D-ITER-EXTEND1 (#3330).

## Current state
- `collect` and `to_list` always return `List` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:266-268,647,893-894`).
- `to_set` is List-only (`:265,654,905`).
- `Set.from([…])` exists but takes a List (`Examples/features/collections/set.jet:12`).
- The only generic static is `Map.fromkeys`/`from_keys` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuiltinStatics.jet:160-161`).
- There is no FromIterator trait. Compiler-owned traits are listed in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Types.jet:77`.
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f017. Operation facts come from #3325 (per #3398).

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - Declare a compiler-owned `FromIterator` trait (`type Item`, `from: fn(source: &&Iter<Item>) -> Self`) beside Iterable/Iterator: add it to `Types.jet:77` and the associated-name table in `Functions.jet:2175`.
   - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuiltinStatics.jet`: add `List.from`, `Set.from`, `Map.from` (items `(key, value)`) and `String.from` (items String or Char) as FromIterator statics that accept any Iterable.
   - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Static.jet`: `T.from(src)` on a user type resolves through its `impl T.FromIterator`.
   - A fallible source (an `Iter` whose items carry `E!`) makes `from` return `T E!`: construction stops at the first error and drops the partial destination.
   - Add routes in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet`, plus JetEval.
2. Host: `jet_set_from_iter`, `jet_map_from_iter` and `jet_string_from_iter` over `JetIter` in `Prelude/Core/Collections.rs`/`Core.rs` and the JIT, plus the Rust mirror.
3. Migrate `Set.from([..])` callers to the protocol form (the spelling is unchanged). Update `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` to document the protocol and the explicit destination rule.
4. Add the example and the UI fixture named in the criteria. The example includes tuple destinations through `unzip`, which is unchanged.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/from_iter Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/set Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` of `from_iter` produce empty diffs.
- The UI snapshot passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: trait resolution and static-call typing.

## Dependencies
None. #3354 builds on this card.

2. The requested destination is explicit at the call; no expected type silently changes a yielding loop or a plain collection map/filter.
3. One construction mechanism handles ordinary and fallible input with the approved partial-result and cleanup law; failed construction does not leak resources.

cards.title: Every project-generated file lives under one top-level `.jet` root, with collision-free project and target identities
cards.body:
Destination: D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B (ratified 2026-09-15): every default project-generated file, build products and generated source included, lives under one top-level `.jet` root at the workspace root (else the package root), reached through one function; no default build/, .jet-build/ or per-member .jet debris; project and target identities never collide or escape; protected saved and audit data survive the migration; `jet doc` writes into the root and never overwrites hand-written files.

Why: scattered generated files pollute source trees and collide across members, profiles and targets (audit 2026-10-28 LAY-01, LAY-03: each workspace member grows its own .jet, about 20 call sites join `.jet` by hand, and `jet doc` overwrote a hand-written docs/index.md).

Shared cache stays under ~/.cache; a ratified package-scoped lock stays where it is.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Every default project-generated file lives under one top-level `.jet` root (D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B, ratified). Project and target identities never collide or escape, and protected saved/audit data survives the migration. Criteria 1 and 3 are verified. Criteria 2, 4 and 5 remain open.

**Current state**
- The build root is `.jet/build`:
  - `Source/CmdCompile.rs:9927` `build_output_root`.
  - `:9931` `bin_path` = `.jet/build/<stem(file)>`.
  - `:9942` `build_artifact_path` uses the bare target name.
  - `:9961` test binaries.
  - `:5314` writes `.gitignore` (`.jet/build/`, `.jet/lock`, `.jet/cache/`).
  - Dependencies are at `Source/Fetch.rs:791,916,1228` (`.jet/build/deps/<dep>`), and exec at `Source/CmdExec.rs:161-165`.
  - No `.jet-build` reference remains in `Source/`.
- Open defects from the 2026-09-23 independent review:
  - Final artifacts collide across entries, profiles, toolchains and targets, because `bin_path` keys on the stem only.
  - Locked preflight compares planned generated modules against all same-member provenance.
  - Action-generated sources get no peer-output overlays.
  - An equal-root package can verify or replace nested-member lock rows as if its scope were global (E3512 shared `.jet/lock` provenance).
  - The first CLI regression used retired `--allow-exec/--allow-fs` flags and tested nothing.
- Other owners: `Source/ReceiptStore.rs` (`.jet/receipts`, canonical target identity), `Source/RecordIndex.rs` (`.jet/records`), `Source/ProveReplay.rs` (`.jet/records/saved/<id>`), `Source/ProductionReceipt.rs` (`.jet/reports`), `Source/RunCache.rs` (the external `~/.cache/jet/run` stays global), and the `Jetpack/Store` port.

**Changes**
1. Jet side: `Jetpack/Store` and `Jetpack/CLI` must use the same `.jet/build/deps` and lock layout as `Source/Fetch.rs`. Mirror any path helper in Jet, and add no second layout.
2. `Source/CmdCompile.rs`: key artifact paths by the ballot's identity: entry (project-relative path for equal basenames), profile, target and toolchain. The default host dev build keeps its current `.jet/build/<name>`, and non-default identities get a distinct subpath. Use one helper for build, test, run and doctest.
3. Lock provenance: scope `.jet/lock` rows per workspace member and limit preflight to the same member (the ReceiptStore/Fetch lock readers).
4. Action outputs: overlay peer outputs for action-generated sources.
5. Cleanup: `jet clean` removes only classified disposable subtrees (`build`, `cache`) and never `records/saved`, `receipts` or `reports`. Update ignore rules together.
6. New `tests/generated_storage_root.rs` using the current authority flags.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test generated_storage_root` → all cases pass.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases build_entry/ --test package_outputs --test comptime_cli_parity` → still green (default `.jet/build/main` layout unchanged).
- A grep for `.jet-build` and a bare `build/` default writer in Source/ and Jetpack/ → no hits.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: this is Source/ CLI path/lock/cleanup code, plus the Jetpack store path mirror.

**Dependencies**
None open. #3415 (history FIFO) consumes this root but does not block it.
cards.checkSteps:
First check the owner-ratified option in D-GENERATED-STORAGE2. Under B, exercise nested entries and workspace members and verify that default build products stay under the same top-level .jet/build/ root. No sibling top-level build/ or .jet-build/ may appear. Check ignore rules do not hide protected saved claims. A read-only case must distinguish optional cache failure from required output failure; do not assume a silent user-cache fallback.

Run rebuilt build/run/dev/test and record operations from isolated standalone and package projects, including a read-only source directory, symlinked path, second target, and concurrent invocation. Compare created files with the classified ownership map, inspect saved/audit links, then exercise selective cache cleanup. Verify another project and unrelated .jet contents are unchanged. Use a bounded cache fixture for failure injection.

Existing focused regression starting points (future commands, not executed; they do not alone cover the new criteria):
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test run_cache dependency_and_argv_invalidate_cache_key -- --exact`

questions.text: Do not like either option. How is this handled elsewhere for other languages? I like the idea of one top level .jet folder that also includes things like build folder for anything generated by jet to keep things clean and tidy without polluting top level dir
questions.answer:
Yes. One top-level .jet directory is a reasonable design. My earlier ballot treated a local directory as clutter, but your concern is scattered directories, not one organized directory.

Other tools handle this in several ways:

- Rust/Cargo puts build outputs in workspace-root target/ by default. It separates profiles and target platforms below that root. [Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-cache.html).
- Dart shares .dart_tool/ for project tool caches. Its build tools use .dart_tool/build/. Downloaded packages remain in a shared user cache. Not every Dart output lives in .dart_tool/. [Dart documentation](https://dart.dev/tools/pub/package-layout#project-specific-caching-for-tools).
- Java/Kotlin with Gradle uses .gradle/ for project caches and build/ for build products. Shared caches also exist under the user's home directory. [Gradle documentation](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/directory_layout.html).
- .NET offers an opt-in artifacts/ directory containing every project's build outputs, grouped by kind and project. This is the closest direct precedent for gathering build outputs under one configurable root. [.NET documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/sdk/artifacts-output).

I revised B to mean one top-level .jet directory for all default project-generated files, including .jet/build/, .jet/cache/, and .jet/generated/. Existing records, receipts, reports, and locks also remain below that root. Nested source files share the root rather than creating their own directories. Default top-level build/ and .jet-build/ disappear.

Generated does not mean disposable. Saved replay claims, required evidence, and reproducibility metadata keep their protection. Routine cleanup and version-control ignore rules must target disposable contents, not all of .jet. Shared downloads, user credentials, application data, and explicitly requested export destinations remain separate.

The retained limitation is write permission: required local build output needs a writable destination. Optional cache and history writes keep their existing best-effort behavior.

I now recommend the expanded B. I updated the ballot and card #3421, but left the decision open for your ratification. No generated files were moved or deleted. The comparisons come from official documentation read on 2026-09-15; they are not newly executed peer builds.

cards.title: Core HTTP client in Jet, including checked header names and values
cards.body:
Owner 2026-09-28: the standard library must be written in Jet under Core/; port whatever the Rust Prelude files still own. Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/prelude-core-gap.json (Opus 5.5 study, file:line citations). Move every semantic item (validation, defaults, formats, protocol logic, limits, error meaning) into the named Core/*.jet home; keep only policy-free provider leaves in Rust (raw syscalls, socket I/O, vetted TLS/SQLite/Parquet/Wasmtime engines). Migrate every route (AOT emit, JIT, interpreter, web where applicable) to call the one Jet meaning (I9) and delete the duplicated Rust policy in the same cutover. Proof needs a compiler build that embeds the edited Core sources, so this is blocked by #3663 (master does not compile) and #3591.

Files: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs.
Homes: Core/http/{client,http,h1,h2,hpack,cookie}.jet. Resolve the retry divergence (Jet retries PUT/DELETE, Rust only safe methods) to one documented rule. Delete dead client-handle builder code and JetHTTPAmbientDeadline::push if no caller remains.

Semantic items (18):
- HTTP.rs: JetHTTPAmbientDeadline / compose_total_deadline (HTTP.rs:18-67) -> Core/http/client.jet
- HTTP.rs: Client limits constants HTTP_CLIENT_DEFAULT_REDIRECTS/UPLOAD_REPLAY_CAP/RESPONSE_BODY_LIMIT/H2 queue caps (HTTP.rs:68-78) -> Core/http/client.jet (C_MAX_REDIRECTS etc. exist; reconcile)
- HTTP.rs: PoolKey/ClientPool/OriginLimits/OriginPermit keep-alive + per-origin concurrency (HTTP.rs:104-276) -> Core/http/client.jet (new pool section)
- HTTP.rs: RetryPolicy/ClientPolicy/ClientHandle + jet_http_client_{new,cookies,redirects,allow_http_downgrade,retries,proxy,proxy_from_environment,protocols,decompression,root_certificate,tls,timeouts,drop,send_with}_impl (HTTP.rs:283-700) -> Core/http/client.jet (Client/Session builders)
- HTTP.rs: CookieJar, StoredCookie, CookieSameSite, parse_cookie_date, days_in_month, days_from_civil, domain_matches, PublicSuffixRules, registrable_domain, is_public_suffix, schemeful_site, default_cookie_path, path_matches (HTTP.rs:704-1118) -> Core/http/cookie.jet (new; Core/http/http.jet has only cookie/cookie_encode/cookies_parse http.jet:771-819)
- HTTP.rs: H2Frame/H2Connection/h2_write_frame/h2_read_frame/h2_header_block/h2_response_headers/read_h2_response/H2BodyReader (HTTP.rs:1180-1660, 3915-4224) -> Core/http/h2.jet (new)
- HTTP.rs: DNSEntry/DNSCache TTL policy (HTTP.rs:1746-1785) -> Core/http/client.jet
- HTTP.rs: http_tls_pem_certificates/http_tls_private_key/http_tls_pem_base64 (HTTP.rs:1842-1941) -> Core/net/tls.jet (shared PEM parser); partial precedent Core/email/email.jet:578 validate_ca_pem + Core/encoding base64
- HTTP.rs: validated_timeout/PhaseTimeouts/resolve_phase_timeout/resolve_request_phase_timeouts/remaining_timeout (HTTP.rs:2088-2166, 3167-3179) -> Core/http/client.jet
- HTTP.rs: jet_http_client_get_parts_impl/post_parts_impl/send_parts_impl/send_owned_impl/send_stream_parts_impl/send_with_stream_parts_impl (HTTP.rs:2167-2530) -> Core/http/client.jet + Core/http/http.jet send_request (http.jet:470)
- HTTP.rs: HTTP_FORBIDDEN_REQUEST_HEADERS/connection_close_value/validate_request_header(s)/validate_request_header_pairs/http_token_byte/http_field_value_byte (HTTP.rs:2531-2588, 3512-3535) -> Core/http/http.jet (valid_header_name/has_ctl exist http.jet:1043,1051; forbidden list missing)
- HTTP.rs: prepare_request_parts(_owned)/coalesce_request_header(s|_pairs)/encode_component/encode_form/multipart_boundary/encode_multipart (HTTP.rs:2589-2644, 5413-5534) -> Core/http/http.jet (form_encode/query_encode exist http.jet:716-769; multipart missing)
- HTTP.rs: send_following_redirects(_upload)/resolve_redirect/drain_redirect_body/redirect_may_replay_body/tee_upload_chunk (HTTP.rs:2645-3020, 3549-3551, 3688-3702) -> Core/http/client.jet (Session-only session_follow/resolve_location/redirect_headers exist client.jet:188,345,389)
- HTTP.rs: select_proxy/no_proxy_matches (HTTP.rs:3021-3078) -> Core/http/client.jet
- HTTP.rs: send_once/send_once_upload/encode_request/write_upload_body/slice_body_reader/write_request (HTTP.rs:3180-3511, 3640-3773) -> Core/http/h1.jet (new)
- HTTP.rs: read_head_bytes(_after)/parse_status_and_headers/header_first/content_length/decoded_gzip (HTTP.rs:3774-3914) -> Core/http/http.jet parse_response/content_length exist (http.jet:474,870); streaming head reader missing
- HTTP.rs: read_response/BodyFraming/ResponseBodyReader (HTTP.rs:4225-4562) -> Core/http/h1.jet (new)
- HTTP.rs: HPACK_STATIC/hpack_integer/hpack_string/hpack_literal/hpack_request/HpackDecoder/hpack_read_integer/hpack_read_string/hpack_huffman_decode (HTTP.rs:5003-5412) -> Core/http/hpack.jet (new)

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):
D-HTTP-HEADER-BAD1=A
HeaderName/HeaderValue are checked text types with RFC token/field-value literal validation; all listed setters/builders require them; dynamic parse returns HTTPError.InvalidHeader and no second runtime validation; invalid written character is actionable compile error; session_retries bounds fail; no silent unchanged-header fallback; valid behavior and all original HTTP client framing/transport acceptance remain.

**Goal.** The HTTP client's meaning moves into Core:
- HTTP/1.1 framing, HTTP/2 framing and HPACK
- cookies with public-suffix rules
- redirects, proxies, pool/per-origin limits, DNS TTL, phase timeouts
- header/form/multipart encoding and retries

It lives in `Core/http/{client,http,h1,h2,hpack,cookie}.jet`. Rust keeps socket I/O, TLS (rustls) and gzip inflate leaves only.

**Current state.**
- `Core/http/` has `client.jet` (518 lines), `http.jet` (1227) and `server.jet` (91). There is no `h1`/`h2`/`hpack`/`cookie.jet`.
- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs` (5534 lines) holds the policy. The card body lists 18 semantic items with line ranges, which this plan keeps:
  - ambient deadline :18-67, limit constants :68-78, pool :104-276
  - client builders :283-700, cookies/PSL :704-1118
  - H2 :1180-1660/:3915-4224, DNS cache :1746-1785, PEM :1842-1941
  - timeouts :2088-2166, send parts :2167-2530, forbidden headers :2531-2588
  - form/multipart :2589-2644/:5413-5534, redirects :2645-3020, proxy :3021-3078
  - H1 write :3180-3511, head parse :3774-3914, body framing :4225-4562, HPACK :5003-5412
- Retry divergence: `Core/http/client.jet:232` `retryable_method` retries GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE/PUT/DELETE, while Rust retries safe methods only.
- `Core/http/http.jet` already has `valid_header_name`/`has_ctl` (:1043/:1051), `form_encode`/`query_encode` (:716-769) and `parse_response`/`content_length` (:474/:870).
- #3663 was fixed in 6fc6f3862.

**Changes (one sub-module per patch).**
1. `h1.jet` (new): request encoding, upload body writing, the streaming head reader, and `BodyFraming` (content-length/chunked/close) readers over a byte-stream leaf.
2. `hpack.jet` (new): static table, integer/string/Huffman codec and the decoder dynamic table. `h2.jet` (new): frame read/write, connection settings/flow control and the response body reader.
3. `cookie.jet` (new): `CookieJar`, date parse, domain/path match, and the PSL `registrable_domain` over a generated constant table (F2).
4. `client.jet`:
   - pool/origin limits, the DNS TTL cache and phase timeouts
   - redirect follow with body-replay rules, and proxy/no_proxy selection
   - reconcile the limit constants with the existing `C_MAX_*`
5. `http.jet`: the forbidden-request-header list and multipart encoding.
6. Retry rule, kept as the one documented rule: RFC 9110 idempotent methods (current Jet `retryable_method`), and only when the body is replayable and no response bytes arrived. The Rust safe-only branch is deleted. Document it in the `client.jet` doc comment.
7. PEM helpers move to `Core/net/tls.jet`, shared with #3666.
8. Delete the ported Rust, the dead client-handle builders and `JetHTTPAmbientDeadline::push` if uncalled, plus the Jet-owned `core.http` dispatcher rows. Regenerate the tables.

**Proof.**
- The commands in add_criteria.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases http/` and `cargo test --test http_dependency_audit`: pass.
- A perf cell is required only if the matched networking battery covers the client. Rerun it and keep the Rust route on any loss.

**Batch.** `batch-core-net`: Core http/net source and its Rust Prelude twin, needing one build and the net retest.

**Dependencies.** None open. It shares the PEM parser with #3666, and whichever lands first owns `Core/net/tls.jet` PEM.

cards.title: Sync engine: query, mutation and action kinds, app.live, one owning module, and the bootstrap and local-only design
cards.body:
Owner note (2026-09-28): "I want a jet-native tool that functions like convexdb as an excellent, world class sync engine" (linked video https://youtu.be/pRf8_40EDtM is Tom Delalande's Linear case study, not a Convex video).

Harvest (mine-for-jet report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28):
- Linear (video 4:12-8:26): the client downloads the workspace once, then every read and write is local; one observable state re-renders views; the engine turns local changes into transactions and streams remote changes over a socket, so local and remote changes look identical; the server accepts or rejects each transaction and the client rolls back on reject; large workspaces forced lazy loading and a partial bootstrap; engineers can switch sync off to prototype locally; there is no plug-and-play engine, and it takes several full-time engineers to maintain.
- Convex (https://docs.convex.dev/functions/runtimes): queries and mutations must be deterministic (seeded Math.random, Date.now frozen per call) so the system can retry and re-run them; non-deterministic work such as fetch lives only in actions.

Jet already ratified most of the mechanism: D-LIVEQUERY1 (footprint-tracked live queries over -[DB.Read]> functions, #Transact write-set invalidation, pushes to Signal<T>), D-EFFDBREAD1, D-SYNC1 (CRDT values over the live channel), D-DBPOLICY1 (row policies below app code), D-DX-QUERY1 (optimistic mutation with rollback), D-DX-SERVERFN1 (typed calls derived from App actions), D-QUERY-LIVE1 (incremental maintenance). Jet's advantage Convex cannot copy: effect rows can prove at compile time that a query only reads, that a mutation is replay-safe, and that only actions touch the network; the same Jet validation code runs on client and server (I9).

Current state is far from that: the shipped example does not compile, Core/app is string-keyed, and app/web duplicate the surface (#3700, #3701).
cards.plan:
**Goal**
A Jet-native local-first sync engine at Convex/Linear grade (owner note 2026-09-28: "a jet-native tool that functions like convexdb as an excellent, world class sync engine"). It covers client cache and partial bootstrap, local reads and writes as transactions, server accept or reject with rollback, socket fan-out, an offline queue and a local-only mode. Query, mutation and action are compiler-checked effect classes.

**Current state**
- Ratified mechanism: D-LIVEQUERY1 (footprint-tracked live queries over `-[DB.Read]>`, `#Transact` invalidation, `Signal<T>` push), D-EFFDBREAD1, D-SYNC1 (CRDT values), D-DBPOLICY1, D-DX-QUERY1 (optimistic mutation plus rollback), D-DX-SERVERFN1 and D-QUERY-LIVE1.
- Code: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Database.jet:31-41 tags `query`/`query_one`/`live` as `DB.Read` and `execute` as `DB.Write`. Effect checks are in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet. Core/sync/sync.jet exists. A read is judged on the stored row, an insert on the new row, a delete on the stored row and an update on both; the policy's reads see the transaction's earlier writes but not the write being judged. A row the caller may not read is never returned. A Member's update of its own member row to Owner is refused. The creator rule admits an Owner member insert only for a project whose row names the caller as created_by and has no members, so create_project makes the caller its owner and nothing else can. questions.text: we already have html type with literal constructor, this seems to overlap and be a duplicate spelling for the same thing.
questions.answer:
You're right. The old option A would have added a second spelling, #HTML { … }, for the same HTML value that HTML{"…"} already builds. I redrafted the ballot so every option ends with exactly one way to write markup in code. The new recommendation, A, keeps the existing HTML literal (including the three-quote form for several lines) and has the compiler check it: unknown tags or attributes and closing tags in the wrong order become compile errors. Holes may also hold a list of HTML values. The unbuilt #HTML block retires; #HTML(page) file pairing stays. B is still bare like JSX, and C is the labeled block. Under B or C the literal retires for markup in code, so neither leaves two spellings either. Builder functions are withdrawn. Today the literal checks nothing: HTML{"

Hi

"} compiles. A fixes that. (The redrafted ballot is with fresh beginner and adversarial readers now; it replaces the posted text as soon as they pass.)

questions.text: Im not sold on why this is a good or useful idea, you just say that python habits work. Are those habits good? What is the CBA?
questions.answer:
Fair challenge: "Python habits work" was the wrong argument. A does not bring in Python's loose typing. The list still holds one type, set by the first line that uses it, and every type is fixed before the program runs. A only saves writing the type twice. Is the habit good? Starting empty and filling in a loop is normal everywhere, but in Jet `names :: people.map(p -> p.name)` is often cleaner and needs no written type.

What A buys:
- One less stop for newcomers. Today's error even suggests `[Int]{}` while Lena pushes text.
- At most about 6,300 written types in Jet's own code: 5,363 empty lists or maps and 927 `None` ("no value yet") starts. Some stay, where no later line settles them.

What A costs:
- Reading: `names := []` no longer says what it holds, and a GitHub review shows no editor hint.
- Error placement: if the first push is the mistake, Jet blames the next, correct line. Today the error lands on the bad push.
- One rule: in Jet a typed value starts with its type, the rule D-ANGLE-CAST2's recommendation keeps. A makes empty lists an exception.
- Work: new checking machinery in the compiler, during the Rust exit.
- Safety and program speed: no change either way.

Verdict: both sides are small, and the costs fall on readers. We now recommend keeping today's rule (B) with a better error: it names the type from the later line, and `jet fix` writes it in. The ballot should be revised to offer that before you vote.

questions.text: Diagnostic follow-on errors (18 UI rows). When the compiler recovers from a first error, should it also report the follow-on errors that recovery causes? The old Rust compiler did, and these snapshots expect them. Examples: E0102 "`Unknown` has no method ..." (the internal recovery type leaks into the text; 7 rows), the same E0927 reported twice at one place (6 rows), and E0107 after an item was already rejected (5 rows). The Jet compiler reports only the root error. No spec line decides this. Options: (A) report only the root error; follow-on errors from recovery are dropped and the 18 snapshots are corrected (Main recommends this: fewer, truer errors, and no internal names); (B) keep the Rust behavior and make the Jet compiler emit the follow-ons. Until you answer, the 18 rows stay known-failing on this card.
questions.answer: Owner (chat 2026-11-01 ~07:50 EST): root error only. Recovery follow-ons are dropped and the 18 snapshots are corrected.

questions.text: Output drift with no spec rule (13 test cases). The Jet tools print something different from what these cases expect, and no spec line decides which is right. Full diffs: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Gold/GoldC/undecided-triage-output.md. Groups: A) a stopped programs error report now adds a "failed here: run (main.jet:3)" line and the source line (2 cases); B) a refused `jet run` shows relative paths and drops the "N problems found" footer (1); C) help text changed wording (5); D) bind error Why sentences changed wording (3); F) the import report adds a "migration:" line (1). For each group: (keep) the new output is right and the expected files are corrected, or (restore) the tools go back to the expected text. Main recommends keep for A and F (more useful, no lost facts) and restore for B (the footer and full paths carry facts); C and D need your eye. Until you answer, these cases stay known-failing on this card.
questions.answer: Owner (chat 2026-11-01 ~07:50 EST): keep the new output for A, C, D and F, and restore B (a refused jet run keeps full paths and the N problems found footer).

cards.title: Authority law: thirteen roots in one table, the word authority, transitive Panic and memory denials, one policy ladder, and contain/harden
cards.body:
Destination: the authority model is one closed table of thirteen roots with FFI language leaves (D-AUTHORITY-ROOTS1=A), read by every checker with no private copy; no surface says capability for permissions (D-AUTHORITY-WORD1=A); Panic and memory denials are enforced transitively and take arguments (D-NOPANIC1=A, D-AUTHORITY-MEM2=A); one policy surface names every audited escape (D-ONCE-GATE1=A); and the package keys `contain` and `harden` work as ratified.

Why: an authority promise that one checker reads differently from another, or that an unknown call can discharge, is not a promise.

Source: the P04 ratified-contract scope (Main's ruling 2026-11-13: the proofs are tests/cases rows, not the proposed tests/ratified suite), with #1566, #1894 and #2846. Sandbox items went to #6930, tags to #6931, crypto to #6925, native sandbox enforcement to #6697 and netrc to #6632.

cards.title: Parallel, deterministic compilation across all cores, with a single-threaded option
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-02: use every core when it can be done reliably and safely; keep an explicit single-threaded mode. Design: per-function (and per-module where needed) jobs for checking, lowering, optimization and code generation over immutable shared inputs, each job producing owned outputs merged in canonical order, so output bytes are identical for any job count. Determinism is proven, not assumed: the stage-2 fixed point and the golden corpus must produce byte-identical outputs with --jobs 1 and --jobs N. Analyses that are whole-program today (registration, effect solving, return-view summaries) need a parallel-safe formulation (phase barriers or worklists over immutable snapshots).
cards.plan: 1. Make every pass per-function and linear (scaling work under way). 2. Immutable shared program state after registration. 3. Job scheduler in the compiler (core.tasks) with canonical merge order. 4. --jobs flag (default all cores, 1 = single-threaded). 5. Determinism gate: jobs 1 vs N byte-identical on the corpus and the self-compile.

cards.title: Prove jet perf on a game-frame workflow: wait attribution, inclusive time, recursion, scoped spans
cards.body: #2997 (profiler source hotspots) and #2487 (frame profiler) are done, but four questions from game-thread profiling are unproven for Jet. Unreal Insights talk (KxREK-DYu70 10:00-12:00): WaitForTasks gaps are attributed to the awaited task by manually aligning timelines; the fix was to start that work earlier, so a frame critical path matters; timer tables show count, inclusive and exclusive time; capture channels and profile build configuration change results; a frame strip coloured against the budget finds hitches first. Jai iprof (DaJWWePhRsM; Win32 re-mine DAJ-12, DAJL-01): time does not bubble correctly to parents of recursive zones, and manually balanced begin/end zones crash or slow down when an early return skips the end; misused manual instrumentation records nothing silently (DAJ-60). Jet knows join edges, spans and budgets at the language level, so each should be answerable without manual alignment.
cards.plan: Write one game-shaped program (a frame that joins a task group, a recursive function, early returns inside core.log spans, a declared D-GAME-BUDGET1 frame budget) and capture it with jet perf on the shipping toolchain. Check each criterion; fix gaps in the existing profiler and trace product, reusing #2528's critical-path computation, with no second recorder.

ToolsJet 2026-10-30: the core of JetLSP's 89 compile errors (#4917 C9) is a missing native-path carrier. JetSemIndex Docs/Collect, Contracts, Doctests and Graph plus 36 JetLSP files import private core.files.runtime.kernel_path_components and use doc_os_path.OsPath, display_span, file_stem_span and from_encoded, none of which exist in Core. Public core.files.path.Path is String-based, so it cannot carry native-byte paths (JetSemIndex Tests/Docs/Graph.jet:70 asserts [47,112,47,255]). This is a design choice (publish an OS-path surface, which is public API and needs a ballot, or keep a tool-local path module), not a mechanical fix.

RustOut7 2026-10-28 (s1): JetLSP has 89 visible errors (private core.files.runtime.kernel_path_components / core.files.host.retained_descriptor imports in 20+ files, positional tuples). jet self lsp is jet_cli_not_ported at JetCli Front.jet:1620. All 54 tests/cases/lsp cases are REFUSED: 41 put the exit: any reason on the comment line, not inline (kit_steps_reason, Tools/testkit/StepsLex.jet:131); 11 hit the testkit read_bytes seam. JetSemIndex: past its 7 surface errors, jet_driver.Driver is missing; SemIndex/Entry.jet is an unported Rust shim calling nonexistent check_file_with_effect_facts / check_file_with_overlays* and an OSPath type, with no callers outside its own tests; Docs/Graph.jet reads physical_path/display/alias/pub_file/loaded_source, which SemaCompilerModuleSource does not have. cards.title: ui and audio subsystems for games and apps in Jet: present pixels, play PCM, read input, no SDL or raylib (D-GAME-PLATFORM1=A)
cards.body:
Destination: Jet programs open windows, present RGBA or palette-indexed pixel buffers at a fixed rate, mix and play PCM audio with low latency, and read raw keyboard, mouse and gamepad input through two independent Core subsystems, ui and audio (D-GAME-PLATFORM1=A), written in Jet and speaking the display and sound protocols directly (D-RAYLIB-DRIVER-LOAD1), with headless recorders for goldens.

Why it matters: the Jet Doom port, and any game or graphical app, needs this without leaning on C libraries (owner direction 2026-10-16); the owner wants no raylib reference anywhere, only ui and app (2026-11-08).

State: Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/RouteAGame.jet opens no window and input is inert; Core/Game/Raylib.jet's play_sound only checks the path.

Source: mine-for-jet V report (2026-10-16); the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation. Game scheduling and tooling moved to the core.game tools card on 2026-11-15.
cards.plan: 1. Survey the native UI host (#4951, #2999) and the existing Jet linker paths for what already presents pixels. 2. Draft and raise the API ballot (module home, Surface.present(pixels), Audio.queue(samples), input event stream). 3. Implement Linux first (Wayland + X11 fallback, PipeWire/ALSA), then Windows and macOS, all inside Core #Unsafe with audit reasons. 4. Example with golden output (headless surface checksum + recorded PCM checksum) on every tier (I5, I9).

log.text: Closed as merged: every open criterion moved to the card that owns its work, each tagged (was #5035 cN): #6701 (4).
Cleaned 2026-11-15: this card is now the ui and audio platform layer (c19, c21, c22). Game scheduling, frame schedule and tooling (c5-c18, c20, c23) moved to #6887.

Owner 2026-11-08: "i do not want any reference to raylib, just ui and app modules." (after: "i do not want a module or subsystem called ray ... it should just be called ui"). Graphics, windows, frames, drawing and input are `ui`; building apps is `app`. No raylib package, module, API naming, symbol or example remains; D-RAY-API1 (raylib names) and the raylib-package plan are superseded. The cutover is owned by #6701. c19 and c22 name the ray subsystem and raylib-style drawing; read them as ui (windows, frames, present, per-window events, gamepads, ui drawing).
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Proof: `git ls-files Core | grep -i raylib` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Ui/` and `--filter Audio/` pass on O0, O1 and O2.

questions.text: Should this be separate from the app/web framework? I think web should probably be a little different but app and our version of raylib should probably be the same, where our version of raylib is like the visual subsystem & our version of miniaudio is the audio subsystem. They should likely be independent modular scalable controllable systems rather than a monolith so more complex situations can be expressed.
questions.answer: Agreed, and the ballot is redesigned around it. Recommended A now has two independent subsystems shared by games and desktop apps. ray, our raylib, is the visual one: windows, frames, drawing and each window's keys and mouse. audio, our miniaudio, is the sound one: devices, raw sample queues and a mixer. Each works alone, and a program can open several of each. core.game (scenes, replays) and gui (widgets) only combine them, with no device code of their own. Headless versions of both serve tests. The web stays separate. B splits input out too, and C is the old single platform value.

cards.title: Compiler architecture review follow-ups: generator gate, gated tool packages, one helper home, one layout owner
