Destination: the findings of the 2026-10-22 architecture review (Docs/audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md) that no other card owns are closed: generators have one freshness gate, every tool package is gated or deleted, Core and the runtime share one internal helper home, layout has one owner, every import is declared, and IR Lint keeps the Core arity rows true.

Why it matters: drift between copies is silent; each of these is a place where a fix in one copy does not reach the others (Pillar 5, Docs/spec/philosophy.md: one home per rule).

The pipeline itself is ratified as D-ARCH-IR1=A (one non-SSA slot IR between the AST and machine code) and is built: JetIR is the only IR, and IR Lint types every op (db30a75783).

Owned elsewhere: the route tables (#6151, #6615 c8), keep-going's second control flow (#4914), the sandbox target and the committed guest wasm (#6366).

Owner directive 2026-10-21: keep both boundaries frozen and rework only the internals. Owner decision 2026-10-21 (sequencing, Split): (1) freeze old-backend work (MIR/LIR/x64 lowering fixes and backend performance) except what keeps self-hosting and the release chain alive; backend golden failures (~85 of 1032 at m-7: MIR lint, optimizer, 58 E2104 lowering gaps) and backend performance are fixed in the new IR; (2) start the single-IR work now in parallel: detailed plan, then the spike (Core + examples through the new IR, go/no-go on speed and identical output, differential vs the old backend); (3) keep porting front end, Core, runtime and CLI to green goldens (837 of 1032 failures are front end, all carried over) - the green front-end corpus is the oracle for the IR move; (4) remove Rust after the goldens are green on the new IR (Rust stays as the reference until then); (5) script ports continue for correctness; the faster-than-original gate is measured on the new IR.

Script compile-time evidence 2026-10-21 (install-m7, --trace): hello-world build 1.04 s (sources 460 ms mostly wait, link 200 ms; no Core source parsed). Tools/ci/TestShards.jet build 4.83 s: load/parse of 48 Core source files 1.37 s (one 11-file parse group 990 ms wall vs 93 ms CPU = waiting), register 0.71 s, sema 1.7 s (bodies 0.62, finalize 0.86), lower 0.34 s, optimize 0.67 s (legality 0.20 + lint 0.25 = verification passes), native lower+object+link 0.31 s. So ~3.8 s of 4.8 s is re-parsing and re-checking the Core modules a script imports, on every first build. D-ARCH-IR1 (one slot IR) shrinks the lower/optimize/native share (~1.3 s); the data-oriented front end shrinks sema; neither removes the per-build Core re-check, which needs checked Core interfaces + Core objects cached per compiler identity (spec: compiler-speed.md build-speed constraints). In-memory O0 removes object+link.

Owner 2026-10-20: build this SOON (after the cleanup), with a detailed plan ready. Scope widened: DATA-ORIENTED DESIGN THROUGHOUT JET, not only the compiler back end. Flat arrays, integer IDs, interning, struct-of-arrays, no per-node or per-item heap allocation, cache-friendly parallel passes: in the lexer/parser/AST, sema facts, the IR, machine code, the runtime (allocator, collections, strings), Core collections, comptime, LSP/incremental caches and the package store. Ultimate goal: 1M LOC/s self-compile (massive gains everywhere); 30 s is an intermediate milestone. The plan must list, per subsystem, the current representation, the data-oriented target, the expected gain, and the proof.

criteria.text: Runtime deadlock (found by TestSpeedLead 2026-11-05): with more running tasks than about (cores+8)/2, nested joins hang. Every thread waits in futex_wait on a task that never gets a worker, because the scheduler adds at most 8 workers to cover blocked waits (Compiler/JetRuntime Scheduler.jet:1097). Reproduced by a testkit pool whose entries each join a child and its resident watcher task, on the AOT and run tiers; JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=256 avoids it. Met when a join on a child that hasn't started yet runs that child on the joining thread (or an equivalent that never deadlocks), a cases fixture nests joins inside a task group whose limit is at least the core count and finishes on O0, O1 and O2, and the testkit's default pool no longer needs its workaround.

questions.answer: Should a library you download at a fixed version be checked once and reused like Core, instead of rechecked every run? cards.title: Install Jet with one tested command: release tarball, installer script and a Nix flake package
cards.body:
Today a new user cannot install Jet. The install page says to use Nix, but the repository flake ships no `jet` package, so the documented command cannot work. This card gives Jet one documented install path that a CI job proves on every release.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, DOC-01): Docs/site/dist/install.html names Nix only; flake.nix exports rust-musl-toolchain and musl-linker, no jet package. The channel is chosen by ballot D-INSTALL1 (drafted, filed when this card leaves `later`).

Related: #4154, #5068, D-SEED-DIST1=A (seed published as a release asset for CI and Nix).

Receives #6068 c7 and c8 (onboarding).

Follow-up to the CI removal (1c820b3b0f): Tools/ci/CiEvidence.jet still hashes .github/workflows/ci.yml as its workflow_hash. It has no in-repo caller now (its case writes its own fixture ci.yml, so the case still passes). It comes back with hosted CI on this card; until then, running it on the checkout reports the workflow hash as unavailable.

cards.title: Core members are declared in Core source; the compiler's twin tables and route tables are deleted
cards.body:
Finding F01 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). The compiler keeps a twin of Core's API. Core members are typed and dispatched by compiler tables (Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet:1-4, CoreCallExtensions.jet; generated Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:10 with 1,998 rows; hand-written Registry/CoreSignatures.jet:88, CorePlatformSignatures.jet:229, CoreHostSignatures.jet:22, CoreValueSignatures.jet). A native row wins over the Core declaration (Sema/Calls/Core.jet:264-270). A package can reach the host only through C FFI.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Add one public declaration for a host-provided function, usable by any package, whose signature, effects, failure and sink facts are read from the declaration. Move every Core member that has a CORE_CALLS row to that declaration in Core source. Delete Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet's member rows, CoreCallExtensions.jet, the generated CoreCallRows table and the hand-written signature tables in one cutover. The spelling of the declaration is ballot A on this card.

log.text: Closed by Main: every criterion is met; each moved to the card that owns its work (#6851 and others), and its blocker #6615 is done.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c14, c15 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

2026-11-14 TowerKeeper-1: split into three streams. This card keeps Core declarations, the twin signature tables, the route tables, CoreReach, core.build and the D-CORE-LOWER1/D-EMBED-TOOLCHAIN1 table work. Core-only privileges (c5, c6, c8, c9, c20, c21, c23, c35, c36) moved to #6851; declaration facts and layout (c18, c29, c30, c32, c33) moved to #6852. c46 restated: D-FLOAT-INT1=A covers scalar conversions, the SIMD bridges stay under D-SIMD1/D-SIMD2.

c18 and c20 depend on #6156/#6157 (G5DevX-1, 2026-11-12). The <corelib>/ key-prefix tests in BuildTypes.jet (about 14 sites, for example lines 33, 399, 547, 561, 598, 3384) and in Sema (about 33) decide runtime-handle layout and Core-only privileges. They can go only once a package-neutral mechanism for both exists, so moving the test into a helper would only dodge the criterion's grep and is refused.

c46 conflicts with ratified D-SIMD1/D-SIMD2 (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4116-4125): [F32#4] bridges through from_array/to_array (E2510/E2511), and Core has 30+ to_array methods in Core/Math (Math.jet:14971..17725). c46 cannot remove them without a newer owner ruling, because by the authority order the ratified decision wins. c46 stays open and unworked until its scope is restated to the to_* conversions outside the ratified SIMD bridge. Source card #6255 no longer exists on the board. c14 (CoreReach names no Core path or helper) needs the demand table derived from Core declarations; it goes to G4Ports-1, which owns CoreReach (c2c, e1384f98cc).

Unlanded work saved from the TLS lane worktree TlsLead-3-6151 (on 73739ba7c3) before it was removed, 2026-11-12 00:15: a Taint rework toward c32 and c33, never submitted. 35 files, +266/-362: Sema/Taint.jet (174 lines), ProveReplay.jet (99), CoreSourceRows.jet (27); it deletes JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Sinks.jet, and touches CoreCalls.jet, CoreRecords.jet, the E0722 docs and about 25 tests/ui/taint goldens. The diff is at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/tls-unlanded/TlsLead-3-6151.patch. It has not been reviewed, built or tested; whoever takes c32 starts from it.

c32 credential sinks: no new marker (that would need a ballot). Sinks are derived from declarations. A credential sink is any call whose declared effect row writes outward (Log, IO, Net or FS writes), plus to_string/to_bytes on an Encode-trait impl. The Taint.jet hand table is deleted. The effect half lands first, then the sink half with a sweep of every Jet source; legitimate releases go through the existing #Secret release path. Taint.jet:315 (core.watcher.process_pid to Exec) goes away with declared destinations.
t18a landed TlsLead-6151c26 (c2cecce162..0a995af312): c26 and c27 met.

t17a landed TlsLead-6151c17 (c17 met), TlsLead-6151c23 (c24 met; c23 stays open: the Calls/Core.jet E0510 host-leaf gates remain until #6615 c5) and TlsLead-6151c52 (e75850d064..c2cecce162). c52 isn't met yet: its ffi and export case lines had red rows. Lander2 traced them to 4 selfhost_terminators jet_lexer cases broken by ScriptAPI-7 (EffectVocabulary's embed_file of toolchain:Compiler/Prelude/Effects.jet gives E0945 when a case copies JetFoundation out of the tree) and a musl race in cffi concurrent-bridges that passes alone. c52 is met when ScriptAPI's fix-forward lands and both lines pass.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). D-FLOAT-INT1 was ratified A on 2026-11-08, so c46 (Type{value} conversions) and c51 are unblocked. Owner gate (2026-11-06): c14, c15, c17, c18, c29, c30, c35, c36 wait for one plain owner question per feature (package-private helpers, layout and lazy lowering, trait-bound format and decode, declaration facts); none is drafted yet.

c46: the conversion question is ballot D-FLOAT-INT1 (what Int{f} means for a Float). Correction to the earlier note: Type{value} is already the ratified scalar conversion (D-DOTCTOR3 amendment, syntax-decisions.md:1214-1239); only Float to Int is open. c46's work (no to_* conversions left in core.math) uses Type{value} or Target.from_source either way.

c46 (conversions), owner note 2026-11-06: owner recalls conversions use the literal constructor form (Int{myFloatVar}). The ratified rule in Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:1122 is D-SHAPE-CONVERT1=A, Target.from_source(value) (Float.from_fraction(f)); no ratified Target{value} conversion form was found. c46 stays open until the owner confirms which form rules; no code changes until then.

Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat, cut questions): "Core plays by package rules" criteria wait. Main designs the public features each needs (package-private helpers, layout and lazy-lowering control, trait-bound format/decode, declaration facts) and asks the owner one plain question per feature; nothing is dropped.

MechB-2 (2026-11-06): c44 and c45 landed in 362a902d3c (12 private to_u8 helpers become the public wrapping(U8{n}); git grep -w to_u8 Core is empty). Not mechanical until #6615 lands: c1, c2 (= #6615 c5), c3, c11, c12 (the D-HOST-LEAF1=E cutover) and c48-c50 (CoreCallRows, Core.jet and signature tables wait for #6615 c4/c5). Waiting on cut rows: c6 (cut c5), c9 (cut c8), c33 (cut c32).

Single-source census F18 (Docs/audits/2026-11-05-single-source-census.md): Builtin method lowering routes. Already owned by #6151 c11, #3325; this is the drift evidence those criteria must clear. One hand-written home: BuiltinMethods.jet rows (plus the runtime export). Fix: gen: put the runtime symbol in the row and derive arity and borrow flags from parameters and access. Drift check: Generator `--check`; `runtime-abi-symbols.mjs` confirms each symbol exists. Drifted on 2026-11-05: Not checked row by row Effort L.

OWNER 2026-10-30 asked what Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet is ('looks nothing like jet ... some weird kind of table or config file'). Facts at dev 216cac590b: 2546 lines in a custom line format, not Jet: 1938 dispatcher_row lines (1791 of them embed literal Rust constructor text, CoreCallRecord::new(...)), 343 ambient_route, 115 module export lists, 113 source_module owner lists, 7 format_row and 4 bootstrap lines. The module, export and owns rows restate what Core/*.jet already declares. It is read by about 10 compiler registry files, Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-core-sources.mjs and Tools/agent checks, and its header still names deleted Rust tables. C2 deletes its member rows; under D-DECL-TYPES1 A (ratified) the remaining runtime-symbol and ambient facts become markers on the Core functions themselves, so the file goes entirely.

Merged #6163 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Build core.build and the fn build host on the public compiler library. Body: Finding F16 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). core.build is implemented inside the compiler: Compiler/JetBuildSession/Source/Session.jet:1-4 (private compiler service linkage), Keys.jet:1-5 (Rust v2 key contract), Declarations.jet:1-2 (Rust runtime_bridge positional contract); Compiler/JetEval/Source/BuildServices.jet:1-3; Build and BuildPlan methods are dispatched by member-name strings in Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BuildAdapter.jet:36-81. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Make core.build ordinary Core source over the public compiler library's typed extension points (#6139). The fn build host calls those functions; delete the string dispatch in BuildAdapter.jet and the private session linkage.

Merged #6162 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core lexes and parses with the same rules as packages (amends #5978). Body: Finding F14 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core is lexed with reserved identifiers allowed (Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/MarkerGroups.jet:222, Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Terminators.jet:558-560) and parsed by its own job with owned members (Loader.jet:3489-3497, 3525). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Give packages the same private `__` name rule #5978 settles for Core, or remove Core's exception; then lex and parse Core with the ordinary job. Fold this into #5978's plan if Main prefers.

Merged #6161 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core calls get effects and sink classes from their declarations. Body: Finding F12 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). A Core call gets its effects and credential-sink class from module-name tables, not its signature: Sema/Taint.jet:240-288 (sema_taint_core_effect) and 290-300 (sema_taint_credential_sink). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Write each Core function's effects in its signature and its sink class with a public marker; read them like a package's. Delete both tables. Coordinate the moved effects with #6137.

Merged #6160 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Copy, resource and typestate facts come from declarations, not Core type names. Body: Finding F11 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Copy, resource and typestate facts come from name lists: Sema/Ownership/Copy.jet:298-307, 597, 697; Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:225; Sema/Typestate.jet:67-68 (Task join and detach). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Declare each fact on the Core type with the public derive, marker or typestate syntax. Delete the name lists and the hard-coded Task transitions.

Merged #6159 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core receives every diagnostic packages receive. Body: Finding F09 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core skips marker vocabulary and site checks (Sema/MarkerModules.jet:439, 447), unbuilt generator and runtime-use checks (Sema/CheckProgram.jet:5005, 5037), typestate validation (CheckProgram.jet:3189-3192, Sema/Typestate.jet:64, 70), budgets (Sema/BudgetSpecs.jet:158-165), a serde pass (Sema/Registration/SerdeItems.jet:1513), and the unbuilt-Core-call refusal (Sema/Calls/Core.jet:218-224). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Remove each exemption. Fix the Core sources the checks then flag, or record each needed exception with the public allowance a package would use.

Merged #6158 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Core follows the same #Unsafe and secret rules as packages. Body: Finding F08 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core reads secret bytes without #Unsafe (Sema/Expressions/Places.jet:752-760, any core.* caller skips E0510). Core alone may wrap a generic formal in ExpiringSecret (Sema/FailureLaw.jet:631) and call ExpiringSecret.new with 3 arguments (Sema/Calls/Static.jet:871). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Wrap each Core read of secret bytes in an audited #Unsafe region. Give ExpiringSecret a public bound that admits Core's generic use, or move the use behind the public API. Delete the three exemptions.

Merged #6157 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Remove constructs only Core may write. Body: Finding F07 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Some record literals, annotations, private native types and protected type names are legal only in Core: Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet:402 with Registry/CoreModules.jet:431; Sema/FailureLaw.jet:549-555 (IOOperation, IOContext, owner annotations); Sema/Registration/Items.jet:3509-3510; Sema/Calls/Methods.jet:1345; Sema/TypeRelations.jet:888 (core.email Limits); Sema/Calls/Core.jet:271 (core_private_seam lets Core reach unexported members). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Replace each with ordinary visibility: private fields or constructors, package-private types, and exports. Delete core_record_literal_is_core_only, the owner-annotation suffix list and core_private_seam.

Merged #6156 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Give every package the lazy-lowering and layout rules Core gets. Body: Finding F06 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Unreached Core bodies are not lowered, but other packages' bodies always are (Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:2643-2661, jet_driver_prunable_core_modules). Core types get runtime handle layouts by identity (Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildTypes.jet:347, 494-504, 538). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Apply reachability pruning to every source module, not only Core. Give runtime-handle layouts a public declaration (F01's host declaration carries the handle type), and remove the `<corelib>/` tests in BuildTypes.jet.

Merged #6155 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Bind format, decode, precise math and line loops through public traits. Body: Finding F05 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Language features call named Core helpers by file path: Compiler/JetIR/Source/CoreReach.jet:35-66 (format selectors to Core/Text/Fmt.jet), 68-82 (__decode_* in Core/Encoding/Encoding.jet), 90-104 (Core/Math/Math.jet precise helpers), 117-138 (`loop line in handle.lines()` to read_line / __stdout_next_line). A user type cannot take part. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Express each binding as a public trait (formatting, decoding, precise arithmetic, line source) that Core implements and any package may implement. Lower the language form through the trait. Delete the path and name matching in CoreReach.jet.

Merged #6154 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Lower Core calls through host-leaf declarations, not IR route tables. Body: Finding F04 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). IR lowers Core members straight to runtime symbols: Compiler/JetIR/Source/RouteHandle.jet (1,035 lines), RouteBuiltin.jet (660), RouteBrowser.jet (509); runtime Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/RouteAFont.jet, RouteAGame.jet, RouteBrowser.jet, RouteTerm.jet, RouteWeb.jet. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: After F01, lower a call to a host-leaf declaration the same way for Core and packages. Delete each route table once its members are host-leaf declarations.

Merged #6153 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Move per-domain call checks out of sema into Core declarations. Body: Finding F03 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Sema has a hand-written checker per Core domain: Sema/Calls/Http.jet (920 lines), HttpRouting.jet (1,167), Services.jet (785), TaskGroups.jet (1,116), StreamHandles.jet (571), ProcessHandles.jet (518), TimeHandles.jet (517), UiHandles.jet (515), Hardware.jet (468), Data.jet (1,564), Geometry.jet (308); Static.jet:871 (ExpiringSecret.new with 3 arguments, Core only). Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: For each file, state each rule with a public mechanism (typed signatures, traits, typestate, marker rules or a library lint) in the Core module it guards, then delete the file. Work one domain per landing; the checklist is the file list above.

Merged #6152 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Replace compiler gates on Core host leaves with ordinary visibility. Body: Finding F02 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Sema refuses some host leaves unless the caller is one named Core module: Sema/Calls/Core.jet:1143-1147 (core.term __stdio_*), 1149-1154 (core.mem.__loader_new from core.data only), 1155-1160 (__coerce_* from core.encoding.json only), 1161-1166 (CSV leaves), 1170, 1268-1272 (global Shared constructor, E0067 outside Core); Sema/Calls/Data.jet:777. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: After F01, declare each gated leaf private to the module or package that uses it, so ordinary visibility refuses other callers. Delete the module-name gates in Sema/Calls/Core.jet and Sema/Calls/Data.jet.

questions.text: I'm confused why this needs an import export market. Why not just have the code? If we use markers then the runtime could be expanded? Why not just have the runtime library be linked in the compiler as a special library? Is there a better way to handle that?
questions.answer:
You're right, and I think your idea beats option A. I'll rework the ballot around it.

Why the boundary exists today: the runtime is already ordinary Jet. It is the package jet_runtime in Compiler/JetRuntime, built once into a native library that every tier links (one runtime, so one meaning on every tier). But Core doesn't use it the way one package uses another. Core calls names like core.time.__sleep_ns, and a table inside the compiler maps each name to a C-style runtime symbol (about 1,000 rows). That table is what card #6151 wants gone. Option A swapped the table for markers and symbol strings. That is still a boundary, just a checked one.

Your suggestion, as a new option E: treat jet_runtime as a normal library that ships with the compiler. Core, and any package, writes `use rt: jet.runtime.time` and calls `rt.sleep_ns(duration.ns)`. There is no marker, no symbol string and no manifest. The compiler reads the runtime's real Jet signatures and effects from its prebuilt package, the way it reads any precompiled dependency. Public runtime functions are the supported surface. Private ones (handle internals, the scheduler) stay unreachable through ordinary visibility, so safe code can't forge or free handles. Effects come from the runtime's own Jet code, so nothing can drop them.

Why it's better: Core then uses only mechanisms any package can use, which is the "language is a library" pillar. And there is nothing to drift, because the declaration is the code itself. Go works this way: `runtime` is an ordinary package. Go's trouble came only from //go:linkname, which reached past visibility into private functions. Swift's standard library uses unchecked @_silgen_name bindings, which is the pattern to avoid.

Costs:
1. The runtime's public functions need real Jet names, modules and types (Int rather than I64, typed handles) instead of jet_std_* C names. That is a cutover of about 575 functions.
2. The compiler must load the runtime's interface from the shipped toolchain.
3. A few runtime helpers written in C keep a C import inside the runtime, under #Unsafe.
#Export(c) stays only for the C ABI that generated code and foreign hosts use.

Next: I'll add E to D-HOST-LEAF1 as the recommendation and attack it in the review (web tier, compile-time evaluation, the layering of the runtime below Core) before asking you to rule.

questions.text: what is considered best practice overall across all domains? we need the correct default with the ability to control exact behavior for experts where needed
questions.answer: Best practice across fields has three parts. (1) The default never loses information silently. IEEE 754 defines float-to-int per rounding direction and signals invalid on NaN, infinity or out of range; Julia's Int(2.5) throws; Jet's own Float{n} already stops when inexact. (2) The rounding is always named, because fields disagree: games want floor for negative coordinates, statistics and money want ties-to-even (the IEEE, Python, NumPy, R, C# and Julia default), everyday arithmetic wants ties-away, and audio and pixels want saturation. (3) Out of range either stops, returns a checkable value, or saturates only when asked. The ballot now recommends A, which follows Julia. Int{f} is exact; trunc, floor, ceil, round (ties away) and a new round_even (ties to even) name the rounding; Int.from_float returns None; a new Int.saturating_from clamps, on every integer head. math.round stops on NaN and out of range instead of today's silent 0 and clamping. The rejected camps are B, truncate and stop (Swift, Python), and C, truncate and saturate (Rust as, Java, Kotlin). There is no unchecked unsafe form, because the range check is one compare that the optimizer removes when it proves the range.

questions.text: Should have a strict check for experts to ensure all is reached to find all errors
questions.answer: Agreed. The one downside the ballot accepted was that an unreached function is only lowered, and its backend fault only found, once something calls it. The rewrite removes that: `jet check` (and `jet build`, per your ruling that both list everything) lowers every function, reached or not, and reports every error in one run; only `jet run` and `jet dev` skip unreached bodies, for speed. If you also want a separate expert switch beyond that, the ballot will show its exact spelling as an option. It goes through a fresh review before it replaces this one.

cards.title: D-HOST-LEAF1=E: the runtime is an ordinary library that Core uses
cards.body: Owner ratified D-HOST-LEAF1 option E on 2026-11-06. jet_runtime becomes an ordinary library: Core and any package write use rt: jet.runtime.time and call rt.sleep_ns(duration.ns). No marker, no symbol string, no hand-written manifest. Internals stay hidden by pub. Amended by the adversarial review (Docs/audits/2026-11-06-d-host-leaf1-option-e-review.md): a declared effect row on a pub runtime function introduces its effects, and the interface is generated from source with the runtime pack. This card builds the runtime side. The #6151 criteria (c4-c41) and #6111 c1/c2 that waited on the host-leaf ballot are unblocked by E and stay on their cards: they remove Core's privileges, which E's ordinary-library model makes possible.

t19 landed TlsLead-6615c4 (0efcf91a49..97462b6d92), the c4 mechanism. A jet.runtime call lowers to the runtime export its interface row names at O0/O1/O2 and in a built binary, and Tools/agent/RuntimeEffectRows.jet --check (in VerifyFull) joins each interface function to its Core leaf by name with 0 differences. c4 stays open until every runtime function Core calls is bound this way (S3 onward).

Main ruling 2026-11-10 on S3, the time cutover (TlsLead3). Under D1 (the carrier projection ABI), each jet.runtime.<module> member is a body-less binding onto the runtime export that holds its one body. The binding is generated from the runtime export rows (the c3 interface), never hand-written, and lowered through a route derived from its Jet signature, so the hand IRRoute rows go. Sema admits carrier types (Option, tuple, List) only for bindings of the generated interface, keyed on its identity, not on a module name; a user `jet.runtime.*` module gets the ordinary C-law errors. The raw exports stay as each function's one far-side body, so they are not a twin, and c8 deletes the dispatcher rows and the compiler twin, not these exports.

Main rulings on the c3-c5 slice plan (TlsLead3, 16 slices, written up in its lane as 6615-plan.md). D1: a jet.runtime call uses the carrier projection of its Jet signature, computed on both sides from the one signature; no exported internal ABI. D2: `jet.runtime.<module>` is the spelling these criteria already name. `jet` is a compiler-provided namespace beside `core` and holds only `runtime`, with no other members. D3: c5 lands one module at a time (S3-S14). A module moves whole, with no dual path inside it, and its dispatcher rows, CoreCallRows, IRRoute rows and RuntimeStopExports go in the same SUB. c5 is met only when the last module lands and a census shows 0 dispatcher_row lines. Finding: c38-c40 on #6151 (core.build) are compiler comptime, not runtime, so jet.runtime does not unblock them.

cards.title: Jet web framework: full breadth and depth parity with the best frameworks, with their downsides designed out
cards.body:
## Outcome

Owner direction: Jet ships a first-class, native web framework (the Core web modules, compiled by Jet, with no JavaScript runtime or wrapped library). It has full breadth and depth parity with every element of the best frameworks, and every known downside of those elements is engineered away in the Jet design rather than inherited. The framework has no brand of its own (D-WEB-NAME1=C, 2026-11-04): it is Jet's web library, named by its module; no repository path or user-facing text keeps a third-party framework's name.

## Scope

Parity is judged element by element against the best framework for that element, not against one framework. The reference set covers at least: TanStack (Start, Router, Query, Form, Table, Virtual, Store, DB, devtools), Next.js, Remix / React Router, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Qwik, Astro, Nuxt, Angular, Phoenix LiveView, Rails (Hotwire), Laravel (Livewire), Django, Leptos and Dioxus, htmx and Elysia/Hono. Elements include routing and typed search params, data loading and caching, mutations and optimistic updates, forms and validation, tables and virtualization, state stores, rendering modes (SSR, SSG, ISR, streaming, islands, resumability, CSR), server functions and actions, real-time and live views, auth and sessions, i18n, images and assets, styling, testing, devtools, error boundaries, deployment and edge targets, and the dev loop.

## Method

1. A dated audit (Docs/audits) with one row per element: the best framework for it, what Jet has (by code path and executable example, not prose), the gap, and each known downside of the best implementation with the Jet design that removes it.
2. One ballot per owner choice the audit raises (new syntax, public API, product behavior), with same-program alternatives.
3. One child card per gap, each closing with an executable example and golden output on every applicable tier (I5, I9), and a performance cell where the element is performance-relevant.

## Known downsides to design out (seed list, the audit extends it)

Hydration cost and mismatch bugs; client bundle growth; waterfalls between nested loaders; cache invalidation by hand; stringly-typed routes and search params; server/client boundary leaks of secrets; framework lock-in to one host; slow dev rebuilds; runtime-only type errors in forms and APIs; opaque magic in file conventions; duplicated validation between client and server.

## Current state

Examples/features/web/tanstack_start/run.jet is a reference app over the Core web modules (router, query, forms, table, virtual, store). Its web build is being repaired under #5990 c13. It is evidence of coverage breadth only; depth parity is unaudited.

log.text: Clarification (Main, 2026-11-16): this card is done only as a container. TowerKeeper-1's board cleanup moved its open criteria to the cards that own the work, and none of them was built when it closed: routes went to #6864, endpoints to #6865, browser tests to #6866, forms, tables and views to #6821, and the parity audit, the one-runtime suite and the one-app proofs to #6445 c12-c18. Only c3, c9, c14, c30, c33 and c38 were met by proof here. The Jet web framework is NOT finished. The open work lives on those cards (all G9).

core.reactive over-notifies and glitches; this blocks c37 (found by GoalsB-5 while measuring reactive_observable, 2026-11-15). An autorun reading n, doubled(n) and plus_one(doubled) re-runs 3 times per n.set(5), and 3 times for n.set(1) when n is already 1 (no same-value suppression). In a diamond (left = a+1, right = a*10, sum = left+right) the effect sees the glitch value 13 before settling. Solid, Vue and Preact signals run once, with no glitch. Fix: a topological or height-ordered propagation, plus same-value suppression in core.reactive. Full notes: the GoalsB-5-16 SUB message.

Cleaned: this card keeps the parity audit (c1, c2, c4, c6, c31), the one-runtime suite (c7) and the one-app and server-call proofs (c35, c36). Routes went to #6864, endpoints to #6865, browser tests to #6866, forms and tables to #6821 (#6821 c3, #6821 c4, #6821 c5).

Shape (Main, 2026-11-14): framework-surface work on this card builds to the ratified D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (#6792, Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md). Every element of that shape has a child card under #6792 (#6799-#6831, #6445, #6447) with executable-example criteria; new surface work here names the shape element it builds and must not contradict it.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Correction to the log above: c14's ballot is not missing. D-DX-BROWSERTEST1=A (ratified 2026-09-04, from #2498) chose "extend jet test" and the spec carries its flags (spec.md:4004-4007), so c14 is met and c15-c18 (scaffold, UI mode, trace viewer, matrix and reporters) are build work inside that contract. Only a new command or a new jet new template name for the scaffold would need its own ballot; adding a browser #Test to the existing web template does not.

BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Body: D-WEB-NAME1=C (2026-11-04) chose no brand, so "its own Jet name" is gone. Owner gates: c14 waits for a browser-test ballot (scaffold, UI mode, trace viewer) that is not drafted; c2 is the standing rule that every audit choice gets a ballot. c30's ballots are ratified and archived with #4282: D-WEBAPP-SERVE1=D (2026-07-28) and D-WEBRUN1=A (2026-08-27). Merged: c21 into c22, c23-c27 into c28, c19 into c29 (D-G9-4, D-G9-5). Gained #5201 c22 (typed forms). New row: the study rerun from the goal body.

Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).

#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 14 criteria from archived #2428, #2472, #2475, #2498, #2852, #2962: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

cards.title: Failure model: three-state outcomes, failure ceilings, visible failure points, dbg and hop trails
cards.body:
Destination: Jet's ratified failure law is built end to end. `T? E!` matches as three states (.Val, .None, .Err; D-OUTCOME-SHAPE1=A, done here). Failures pass up by themselves and None never does. A written failure contract is an optional ceiling and failure sets follow the effect law (D-FAIL-PUBSIG1=A, D-FAIL-EFFECT1=A). Readers see failure points through tools, and teams may require marks (D-FAIL-VISIBLE1=A). A function names its own error cases (D-ERR-CASES1=A, D-FAIL-INFER-UNION1=A). `dbg` works in pure code (D-DBG1=A). `err.as<T>()` recovers a typed failure (D-ERR-TRAIT1=A).

Why it matters: failures are the most common control flow in real programs; each gap here is a place where a beginner writes a conversion by hand or an expert cannot see where a failure leaves.

Spec: Docs/spec/spec.md failure sections; probes: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3838/.

Owned elsewhere: the editor's faint `?` inlay hint (#4917), publish's failure-set version rule (#6860).
cards.plan:
1. Patterns on `T? E!` accept `.Val(x)`, `.None`, `.Err(e)` directly; exhaustiveness over the three.
2. Nested `.Ok(...)` form: greenfield cutover — migrate all sources; the old form gets no teaching diagnostic or jet fix (owner order).
3. Failures keep automatic pass-up; None never leaves a function unless written (`?` on the optional) or `.or_err("why")`.
4. `??` resolves either state.
5. Optional internal single-tag layout only with a paired perf cell.

cards.title: HTTP caching for pages and assets: Cache-Control, ETag and immutable hashed assets derived from facts
cards.body: Gap card for #6792 c6/c7 (owner order 2026-11-13: one cohesive package covering everything a web app and a native app need, with styling far better than HTML and CSS). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md. log.text: All criteria met (p222 batch compiler, dev 18bc53b3e6). Closed by Main.

Implementation decision (Main, within the ratified CachePolicy and .cache<V> surface, no new spelling): sema lowers .cache<V>(policy) to __cache(reply_type: "V", policy), as .screen lowers to __screen. Every GET page or #App.Public endpoint whose reply type is V gets public, max-age plus an ETag; a matching If-None-Match gets 304; the server keeps the encoded reply for max_age, so false, 0 and empty text stay hits (c3) and freshness runs through the expiry instant (c4). #App.SignedIn replies always get private, no-store (c1). c5's shared store is pending Main's reading of D-NEST-UPSTREAM1 (is a store in the app's own database file app-owned?). Speed-3-3 builds c2, then c3, c4 and c1.

cards.title: app: server jobs, the after-commit outbox and schedules (#App.Job, #App.Every, app.enqueue)
cards.body: Gap card N2 from the #6792 r3 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md, section 4.14; crewboard/Logic/crew.jet tell_assignee, send_invite, remind_due_today). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

log.text: All criteria met (p222 batch compiler, dev 18bc53b3e6). Closed by Main.

Ballot D-JOB-STORE1 posted (blocks c9): rec A, no public job-store slot; jobs stay in a core.db store's outbox in the call's transaction, and c9 is reworded to that contract. Main added B's best case (Redis or a cloud queue: job load off the DB, independent scaling) and A's cost (job rows share the database).

p209: c2 (9fb22f4c60) hangs every served mux. Server.jet mux_serving relied on list remove(0, .Slot) giving None on an empty list, but .Slot stops on an out-of-range index (E3010), so the serving task dies at its first serve and the client times out. That broke about 100 suite rows (HTTP examples, web_app, http_server_lifecycle, ws, tls, canvas). Speed-3-2 sends the fix first in p210, sweeping every .Slot ?? return|default caller (App.jet:995, Db.jet:2178). c1, c2, c3 and c4 proof rows fail on p209 for this root.

c9 ruling (Main): a queue store adapter can't be written by user code today. The only adapter seam is core.app's priv(package) transactions module with CallOutbox (Core/App/App.jet:775, :836), joined only by core.db (Core/Db/Db.jet:1362). Refusing a service with #App.Job methods that holds no db.Store would contradict the ratified text in core-library.md:5664-5665 (a call that used no store runs the job at once without keeping it), so that reading is rejected. c9 has a subject only once a public adapter surface exists, and adding one is owner-gated public API. c9 is blocked on a ballot for it; Speed-3-2 moved to #6800 c1.
Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): c1 split; the per-send keys are #6825 c10.

criteria.text: Jobs are kept only in a core.db store's outbox, in the transaction of the call that queued them. core.app has no public job-store slot, so no app code can weaken the contract. Every engine core.db opens passes the contract rows of c1, c6, c7 and c8, and the case states the in-memory case: jobs last as long as the rows that queued them.
criteria.evidence: p222 batch compiler (dev 18bc53b3e6): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/job_store_contract_per_engine PASS 1/1 (2bbb2acc1a)

criteria.text: Each push a job sends gets its own key, made from the run key, the recipient and the send open: or link: value, sent hashed to fit each transport limit. app.notify passes it to the transport: APNs apns-collapse-id, FCM android.notification.tag on a non-collapsible message, and Web Push Topic header and notification tag. A retried run repeats each key even when its query returns rows in another order, so a repeat replaces its earlier copy, and two different sends from one job never share a key.

cards.title: Enum case metadata in the typed reflection path (D-ENUM-CASEMETA1)
cards.body:
Destination: a program reads an enum's cases, their names, payload fields and markers, and a value's active case, through the same typed reflection records as every other type, with zero cost for programs that do not reflect. Why: codecs, UI builders and tests all need case metadata, and a second path would drift.

Governing decisions: D-ENUM-CASEMETA1=A, D-NAME-REFLECT1=A, D-ONE-SHAPE1=A, D-META-REFLECT2=A. The general typed reflection records are built on the reflection card (see the 2026-11-14 log). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement ratified D-ENUM-CASEMETA1=A inside the existing reflection model: typed `TypeInfo.cases` descriptors and the runtime active-case projection `value.case()`. Type-only metadata stays erased and payload values stay typed. No enum-only library, visitor or runtime registry.

## Current state
- Enum TypeInfo is built by `sema_comptime_reflection_enum_type_info` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:1395-1449`). It puts variants in the generic `fields` slot as `FieldInfo` rows (`sema_comptime_reflection_enum_variant_info`, :1129-1155) whose `ty` is a display string (`"Unit"`, the payload type name, or `"{a: Int}"`, :1118-1127). There is no `cases` field or `CaseInfo` row, and no canonical wire name.
- Typed accessors are limited to `has_marker/implements/has_method` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Reflection.jet:132-155`). Codegen and eval mirror that list (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ReflectionMethods.jet:19-22`, `Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet:11-15`). There is no `case()` projection anywhere in Compiler/ or `Core/reflect`.
- Criterion 1 (owner ratification) is met. The scope extension (2026-09-21) asks for a typed descriptor for every type family or a precise refusal, with no fabricated empty catalogs.

## Changes
1. `Reflection.jet`: add `CaseInfo` rows under a `cases` field. Each row carries identity, source name, canonical wire name (serde markers), index or discriminant, group, ordered payload shape (`Unit`, tuple or named) with typed payload `TypeInfo` references, and markers in source-versus-expanded order. Rows are derived from `EnumDef.variants/groups/payloads`. Stop emitting variants as `FieldInfo`. Non-enum types return a registered refusal for `cases`, not an empty list. Generic enums describe the instantiated arguments.
2. `Calls/Reflection.jet`: type `TypeInfo.cases`, the `CaseInfo` accessors and `value.case()`.
3. `ReflectionMethods.jet` in codegen and eval: `value.case()` returns the active case identity plus typed payload fields through one Prelude helper. It does complete-or-refuse capture, refuses shared or noncopyable graphs, and follows copy rules. A program that never reflects emits no case table and allocates nothing.
4. Layout and ABI facts (discriminant width, payload offsets) come from `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/Layout.jet` for the selected target.
5. Archived crates (`jet-foundation/Reflection.rs`, `jet-comptime/Reflect.rs`, `core_types.rs`, `jet-codegen/TIR`) are not edited.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden reflection/enum_cases`: a new example covers unit, named-payload and tuple cases plus one generic enum. It prints `cases` and `value.case()` identically on O0, O1 and O2.
- `jet test Compiler --profile ui reflect_cases_non_enum` covers the refusal.
- Generated Rust for a non-reflecting enum program contains no case table (criterion 12).

cards.title: Markers, effects, facts, derives and tags are ordinary declared types (D-DECL-TYPES1)
cards.body:
Destination: Jet has no special declaration words for markers, effects, facts, derives or tags. Each is an ordinary struct, enum or impl of a Core trait (Marker, Effect, Fact, Trait.Derive), so one mechanism, one reader and one set of tools serves all of them, and libraries declare their own on equal terms with Core.

Governing decisions: D-DECL-TYPES1=A (2026-10-30), D-TAG-MARKER1=A, D-FACT-MARKER1=A, D-DERIVE-PROVIDER1=A, D-MARKER-INBODY1=A (built by #6562), D-MARKER-MODULE1=A, D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1=A, D-MARKER-LAW1=A, D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1=A, D-DECL-COLON1=A. Owner orders: retired declarations get no teaching diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule (2026-11-06); Jet's own diagnostic types live under the `jet.` prefix (2026-10-30).

Decided without ballot (Main 2026-11-11): wrap is typed with the existing Code value and lowered through root-authorized Compiler events and Meta.Rewrite; library combine is as already ratified (no package marker sets resolution). Package settings take ordinary markers on the package settings record (a header in package.jet, the same marker on an inline package record); no inner-marker sigil. Marker struct form: `struct X { fields; impl Marker { settings; fn expand(self, target: Target) { template } } }`; a trailing list field without a default is variadic.

Carried from #6039, #4276, #4284 and #3662 (closed 2026-11-14).

cards.title: Reflection reads typed facts: callables, declarations, fields, markers and run-time views
cards.body:
Destination: every reflection read in Jet returns a typed record from one checked fact path, so a library can read a function's parameters, a type's fields, a marker's arguments or a run-time value without parsing strings. This is the reading half of the metaprogramming ladder (D-META-LADDER1=A) and what markers, derives and fn build all stand on.

Governing decisions: D-META-REFLECT2=A (the TypeInfo, FieldInfo, FunctionInfo records; TypeId identity; PreparedValue), D-PREP-SURFACE2=A, D-MARKER-REFLECT1=A (a marker reads as the typed record its declaration describes), D-REFLECT-FIELDTYPE1=A (field.type is a TypeId). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.

Decisions already taken for this work (Main, 2026-11-11): PreparedValue is a public enum mirroring the compiler's compile-time value cases (Int, Float, Bool, Char, String, Enum, List, Struct, Unit); TypeId is the TypeInfo identity; SourceSpan gains its file; SettingOrigin adds Build beside Declaration, Profile and CommandLine because fn build writes settings. A guard refuses a String-typed reflection field wherever a typed value exists. Fact reads are compile-time only since 4328d5ff94, so run-time examples read them through #run.

Carried from #3520 (closed 2026-11-14) and #6039 (closed 2026-11-14).

log.text: All 18 criteria met; c11 owed-row MetaSuite check landed af0db1d3e1 and passed on p227 (dev eab1677096). Owed rows tracked on #6947 c4 and #6418 c154.

p210 status (D-PRIM-ANY1 round 10 probes): reflect.of on a private type held as a trait value now reports Secret and path n05_private_type_trait_value.lib.Secret (p209 gave M3LibSecret), probably from #3147 n14's ledger paths (9d83b463cd). c16 may now hold; rerun probes n09 and n13 on the next batch compiler before meeting it. c17 is still open: n16 prints the mangled M3GeoPoint.

J34 (C-to-Jet callbacks) has no passing witness until #6947 and #6945 are built; J35 (native jet build --lib) has none until #6418 and #4833. c11 stays open on those cards; every other row passes once GoalsA-1-4-typevalues-meta-suite lands. That SUB also fixes a jet fmt defect from the corpus fmt cutover (28ce99130b): fmt rewrote a bare-name field into name: name, which changed meaning in 8 corpus lines (TypeValues among them). The formatter now keeps bare-name fields, and the 8 lines are restored.

p188 (dev 953b842367), 2026-11-15: c7's Reflection golden group has 79 rows, 3 failing, all TypeValues (E0303 'Struct literal for Type has no field Rock' at TypeValues.jet:40:16, the same on p187). c11's meta_suite is down from 48 coverage problems to 8: ui code_value_paste_takes_a_string and code_value_has_no_register_expansion (snapshot mismatch), plus KNOWN-FAILING J34/J35 witnesses owned by other cards (jet inspect bind and native C callbacks, jet build --lib). GoalsA-1-4 owns TypeValues and the two snapshots.

Decision for c11 meta_suite (Main, 2026-11-15): the Jai families J34 (C-to-Jet callbacks) and J35 (dynamic-library exports) list their real witnesses (cffi_named_pure_callback, Examples/Interop/FFI/Callbacks, the library_outputs cases), so meta_suite fails truthfully on those rows until #6947 and #4833/#6418 land; partial witnesses do not stand in. c11 depends on those cards.

p184 proofs (dev 61b4ee98a7): golden CallableCatalog fails at o0/o1/o2 with E0118 (name bound already taken, run.jet:165), and golden DeclarationFacts is an ICE (exit 101). ReflectionRungs ICEs on p183 and p184 (comptime.build unlowered: argument type TypeInfo) but runs on p182, so it is a regression from p182 to p183; suspects are e90813862d typeid-signature and bce840440f core-bodies-load. GoalsA-1-4 is fixing all three as one SUB ahead of reflect-value.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-15, within D-META-REFLECT2=A), for c2: one typed record per declaration kind, not a single DeclarationInfo. definitions() entries carry a closed DeclarationKind enum in place of the String kind (fixed by the grammar; its row goes in the closed-list kernel ledger as grammar), plus identity and scope. TraitInfo, ConstantInfo and SettingInfo gain identity and scope. ProgramInfo.complete() reports completeness next to the revision. Owner: GoalsA-1-4. c1 SUB GoalsA-1-4-typeid-signature (TypeId.signature gives the CallableSignature) is queued for the next batch.

Handoff (PrecompiledCore-5 stopped, agent cap): SUB g6-callable-fact is in census222 and does not by itself meet c1. Left for c1: function types read one typed callable fact (D-META-REFLECT2). Planned shape: add signature: CallableSignature? to TypeId (CoreRecordRows TypeId row, JetIR CompilerOwned.jet:183, FactReads.jet:631); in Reflection.jet type_id and written_type_id, build it from Type.Fn's params, ret, effect_bound, param_contract and call_metadata, and add it to type_id_record; the other TypeId makers are BuildAdapter.jet:247/289 and Derives.jet:2121; then the spec text at metaprogramming.md ~562 and a fn-typed parameter read in CallableCatalog.

criteria.text: FunctionInfo, MethodInfo and function types read one typed callable fact: parameters with labels and defaults (never run), declared and inferred effects, captures with ownership, access and type, and specialization identity. The callable example reads every field with no string parsing, and changing a callee's signature re-checks code that reads it.

cards.title: Typed routes: checked paths and search params, loader boundaries and route data freshness
cards.body:
Destination: a route declares typed path and search parameters, a loader and its navigation contract; a wrong route or parameter is a compile error; a loader's pending, error and not-found states render; and route data stays fresh by the compiler's read sets.

Why it matters: routing and data loading are the spine of every web app; untyped routes are the most common source of broken links and stale pages.

Decisions: D-ROUTE-ONE1=A (one route table on web.app()), D-ROUTE-FILES2=A (page file words become the address), D-INVALIDATE1=A (the compiler decides what a write makes stale), D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A.

Source: #6552 c8, c10, c11, c12 (from archived #2472). Parent: #6552.

log.text: All 5 criteria met; the last, c4 (capability boundary E2823/E2824), passed on p229 (dev 8c9859caba).

c2 SUB Speed-3-3-6864-c2-app-navigation (queued p226) builds client navigation on web.app()'s one route table: App gains navigate, settle, abort, navigating and shown; core.web.router gets no second public API (D-ROUTE-ONE1=A).

c2 design (Main): route loader boundaries go on web.app()'s one route table (D-ROUTE-ONE1=A: only page rows join client navigation), on the screen routes c1 defines; a loader/settle/show API on core.web.router would be a second route mechanism (I8). Speed-3-3's router-level SUB was returned for that reason.

criteria.text: A screen's route is its state struct (typed `:field` path parameters and `#App.Query` search parameters), its view is the loader, and url_of, go and current are its navigation; a link or navigation to an unknown route or with a wrong parameter type is a compile error with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: p223 batch compiler (dev a8b53c68d8): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter web_route_ PASS 4/4 (2ee79b3cf2)

criteria.text: A route loader's pending, error and not-found boundaries render, and an aborted navigation cancels its preload, on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072), commit 5e327e8133: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/RouteLoaderBoundaries PASS 6/6 (Native o0/o1/o2 and Web); navigation lives on web.app()'s one route table.

criteria.text: Route data is keyed by its route and arguments, turns stale when a write meets its read set (D-INVALIDATE1=A), refetches, and is dropped after its last screen leaves.
criteria.evidence: p225 batch compiler (dev 1b2c2d0a54), commit e05ccf100e: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/route_data_lifecycle PASS 1/1 (O0, O1, O2 and web in the case).

criteria.text: Browser code that uses a server-only capability, or server code that uses a browser-only one, is refused at the app boundary with a registered diagnostic, one UI snapshot per rejection kind.
criteria.evidence: p229 batch compiler (dev 8c9859caba), commits 46a7723059 + e3a2ca03a5: jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter web_capability_boundary_ PASS 2/2 (E2823 browser_reaches_database, E2824 server_uses_browser); the check reads each body's own uses over call edges, so cases WebApp/enqueue_takes_one_job_call and WebApp/live_takes_one_remote_call PASS (no false positive); Tests/Guards/diagnostic_registry_ratchet.jet PASS (p227); full suite p229 has no new failures from it.

criteria.text: Conflicting routes give a deterministic two-span error (E2804); Mux, router and App pick the same handler; HEAD and typed path failures are recorded. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_route_ambiguous_overlap` and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter net/route_overlap`.
criteria.evidence: dev 0b58edf739, gate-p176 jet: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/RouteOverlap gives 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2). The golden tests/run/Net/RouteOverlap.jet records HEAD running the GET handler, a typed path mismatch as 400, and 405 with its Allow list; Router, App routes and marked mounts share one HTTPMux and pick the same handler. jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_route_ambiguous_overlap gives 1 PASS (E2804, two spans). The card's original golden filter net/route_overlap named no row; the golden's path is tests/run/Net/RouteOverlap.jet.

cards.title: Live queries scale: shared results, per-server caps, cross-server invalidation and SQL-narrowed read sets
cards.body:
Destination: live queries (D-LIVEQUERY1=A, app.live) stay correct and cheap as subscribers and servers grow: results are shared when they can be, capped and coalesced when they burst, invalidated across servers, and narrowed to the rows they read.

Why it matters: a live query that re-runs for every subscriber on every write does not survive real traffic; one shared wrongly leaks data between callers.

Decisions: D-LIVEQUERY1=A, D-INVALIDATE1=A, D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A. Gaps K3 come from the #6792 review round 2.

Source: #3709 c13, c18-c21, c24, c25. Parent: #3709.

log.text: Every remaining criterion is met; c12 (warm coverage per screen) moved to #6981, the D-WARM-SET1 ballot it waited on.

c12 waits on the owner ballot D-WARM-SET1 (card #6981): how an app names the reads a device keeps warm. Recommendation A, a warm function in .offline(.Queue, warm: fn ...) checked at compile time against each offline screen's live reads.

c4: Speed-3-3 SUB c4-live-invalidation-across-servers (per-file version map plus a 1 s poll in core.db, two processes, no broker) is queued in p215. The Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-up remains: Core has no Postgres client and the test host has no Postgres, so that half waits on a Core Postgres client stream.
c12 waits on the warm-set ballot (sync note §5.1, ballot B1: proposed, not built, never filed). The orchestrator files it; Speed-3-3 moved to c4.

Blockers (GoalsB-5-2 audit, 2026-11-15): c6 waits on app.caller (#6445 c4, now being built by GoalsB-5-2 on the ambient task caller from #6869 c3); c4 needs a Postgres broker and Core has no Postgres client; c5 needs the SQL-filter Query of D-DB-TABLE1, which is not built; c7 needs app.presence, which does not exist.

Status (GoalsB-5-2, 2026-11-15). c3 submitted: a server-wide re-run cap of 1000 per second, with holds that tell watchers after_ms; 1024 bindings; writes between reads coalesce into one re-run. Design ruling (Main): coalescing between reads plus a cap hold replaces the proposal's fixed 50 ms window, because a fixed window adds up to 50 ms to every live update and changes existing event output. Blocked: c4 (Core has no Postgres client for LISTEN/NOTIFY); c6 and c7 (app.caller() and app.presence() arrive with the #App.SignedIn screens, as #3709 c27/c28 do; the row-policy half of c6 already works per user in db_policy); c5 waits for D-DB-TABLE1 typed table queries (#6822), which GoalsB-5-2 now builds.

Decision (Main, operational, within D-LIVEQUERY1): app.state was E1123 on wasm because Live.run is a rowless fn() -> T E!, so state's solved row was unbounded. Live.run and the bind/poll runs are bounded to -[DB.Read, Net, Time]>, which keeps D-LIVEQUERY1's named sources (DB reads, Net fetch, time polling) and lets web build; a live source with any other effect is refused with E0740, whose fix text names the accepted sources.

Parked 2026-11-15 01:55 by owner order (finish Precompiled Core, the speed plan and the memory kernel before goal work). GoalsB-5 moves to #6759. Landing: GoalsB-5-22r2 (c10) and -23r2 (c2), finished, in census181. Open and unworked until the three are done: c11's livelock bound landed as GoalsB-5-24 (in census180, proof on p155); the rest of the card.

c8 is not met yet, though db_scope_live_marks_writes_stale_only_after_commit passes on p152: the second sync review (2026-11-15) reads App.jet state (L404-416) then live_store (L566-584), which clears dirty unconditionally, so a re-run that read before a commit and stores after its invalidation keeps the old value as current. GoalsB-5 adds a per-binding generation counter and a case forcing that interleaving.

criteria.text: A live query over a tracked source updates from real deltas, a no-op write leaves the cached result untouched, a write publishes only after its transaction commits, and cancelling the subscription ends its re-runs, on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: 68be2c34f4 and 7141a40239: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_lifecycle passes (2 of 2) on batch compiler p182 (dev 9003020128).

criteria.text: A live query that reads no caller-dependent input shares one result among all subscribers with the same arguments.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-23r2 landed b0acab4afa (proof case: a live query that reads no caller-dependent input shares one result). on batch compiler p156 (dev aa5f5f1bba), 2026-11-15 02:03: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_shared_result PASS 1 (it failed on p155, which lacked 22r2).

criteria.text: Each server caps live subscriptions and re-runs per second and coalesces bursts of writes into one re-run. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_caps_and_coalescing` (a load case).
criteria.evidence: 96f6bd2767: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_query_caps_and_coalescing passes (1 of 1) on batch compiler p182 (dev 9003020128).

criteria.text: Invalidations reach subscribers on other servers: a write on one server invalidates the matching live reads on every other server that shares the store, on O0, debug and release.
criteria.evidence: p221 batch compiler (dev 88dc8f59b9): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/live_query_cross_server_invalidation PASS 1/1 (O0, debug, release); still passes in the p222 suite

criteria.text: Predicates the compiler can turn into SQL narrow the read set; any other predicate falls back to table-level invalidation, and `jet inspect` shows which.
criteria.evidence: p219 batch compiler (census build of dev 1123bf884d, Speed-3-3-p215-G-live-filter-comptime landed as 1f51921bea): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/live_query_read_set_narrowing PASS (it failed on p218; the comptime prefetch of a live: local now keeps its SQL filter)

criteria.text: A caller-dependent live query (one that reads app.caller() or runs under a row policy) is not shared between callers; the cost, one re-run per subscriber per write that meets the read set, is measured under the per-server caps.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p187 (dev 9860836a00), 2026-11-15: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/caller_dependent_live_query_is_not_shared 1/1 PASS (landed 7439dda142)

criteria.text: app.presence counts only accounts whose last read of that screen passed its policies: a refused reader is not counted.
criteria.evidence: p221 batch compiler (dev 88dc8f59b9): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/presence_counts_only_admitted_readers PASS 1/1

criteria.text: A write inside a database transaction marks the live bindings over its table stale at the commit or rollback, never at the statement. A binding re-run on another connection while the transaction is open keeps no pre-commit result as current after the commit, and a write outside a transaction marks them at once.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-19 landed 5fa1fd1c85 (marks at commit) and GoalsB-5-21 landed 2ded9a1ded (per-binding generation: a re-run an invalidation overtakes stays stale, review G36). on batch compiler p154 (dev 31ee594ec7), 2026-11-15 01:30: --profile cases --filter live_rerun_overtaken PASS 1; --filter db_scope_live PASS 3; --filter sync_crdt/ PASS 3; golden --filter AppLive PASS 3. The livelock bound is c11.

criteria.text: The WebSocket live hub sends an invalidation only to connections holding a subscription it affects, whose caller passed that source's policy. No event, live or replayed on join, carries another caller's encoded key, and a WebSocket route that reads no live query receives no live event. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/live_hub_events_reach_only_admitted_subscribers` (a two-account case plus an unrelated route).
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-20r2a landed fad05cd5f6 and GoalsB-5-20r2b landed 1e0820d052 (live events reach only connections watching that binding). on batch compiler p155 (dev 49836bd978), 2026-11-15 01:45: --profile cases --filter live_hub_events PASS 1; db_scope_live PASS 3; RuntimeGenerators --check exit 0.

criteria.text: A read-only parameter passed to app.live or app.invalidate is copied or borrowed by the lowering, not moved. Today (p153) the repro (a live source fn count(project: String), with bind and refresh taking project: String) reports E0120 ReadOnlyValueNotOwned at both call sites, and its fix names the compiler temporary __jet_live_N_0, a name the user never wrote. Proof: a case where jet check passes and jet run prints loaded 3; the case live_rerun_overtaken drops its project.copy() workaround.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-22r2 landed dcf8af1eb2 (app.live, subscribe, push and invalidate take a read-only parameter as an argument with no E0120; Live.jet back to 19 copies). on batch compiler p156 (dev aa5f5f1bba), 2026-11-15 02:03: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter live_calls_read_a_read_only_argument PASS 1; the copy ledger ceiling holds (guards 171/0).

criteria.text: Overtaken re-runs are bounded (sync review 3, G86): under sustained writes to a table a live binding reads, the generation rule (2ded9a1ded) does not re-run the source on every read forever. After a stated bound, the binding settles: it serves a value marked stale, or stores one as current with its generation. Proof: a case with a writer loop that invalidates continuously and a reader that reads N times, where the source runs a bounded number of times and the reader gets a value each time.
criteria.evidence: GoalsB-5-24 landed 8630ccf4dd (from the second overtaken run in a row, a binding serves its stale result for a hold of max(run time, 100 ms), then re-runs). on batch compiler p155 (dev 49836bd978), 2026-11-15 01:45: --profile cases --filter live_binding_under_sustained_writes_settles PASS 1; live_rerun_overtaken PASS 1; golden AppLive PASS 3.

criteria.text: Test-host network abilities (sync review gap G64): the app test host can disconnect a client from the server and restore it mid-test, deterministically, so offline, catch-up and replay cases run without real network faults. Proof: a case that disconnects, writes on both sides, restores, and checks the merged state. (was #3709 c28)
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072), commits b9fbc7793e and 2fe268264c: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter disconnected_client_merges_after_reconnect PASS 1/1 (the app test host disconnects a client mid-test, both sides write, the client reconnects and the merged state is checked).

criteria.text: Closing a live connection ends that account's presence on the screens it held: the runtime hub hands a leave signal back to Core (ws_hub_leave), so app.presence never counts a closed session. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/presence_ends_when_the_connection_closes`, on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: p216 batch compiler (census build of dev efb3da4f6c): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/presence_ends_when_the_connection_closes PASS

cards.title: jet new adds services, routes, jobs and migrations to an app, with preview and undo
cards.body:
Destination: inside an app package, `jet new` generates a service, a route, a job or a migration from explicit inputs, shows a preview first, and can undo what it generated from its receipt. Generated code uses the ratified app APIs (D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A: #App.Job, app.enqueue) and the migration CLI (D-DX-MIGRATE1=A), and compiles as written.

Why it matters: generators are how most people start a backend feature; generated code that does not compile or cannot be undone teaches the wrong shape.

Source: #5985 c16-c19 (archived #2458 c1-c4, re-added by the 2026-11 precut audit as unproven). Related: #6825 (jobs), #6552 (web framework).

cards.title: #Inline(Always) is a guarantee, not a hint: every direct call is inlined on every tier, or sema refuses it
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-15: "#Inline(Always) must be a guarantee not a hint". Today (dev d304f826ac) it is honored only at O1/O2 and only when the inliner agrees: OptInline.jet runs at O1 and O2 only, so O0 (jet run, jet dev, compile-time code) never inlines a marked call; the `inline: off` build option and `--inline=off` drop marked inlines too; and the inliner silently keeps a marked call when the callee writes a parameter, is a last-owner routine, reads context.trace, has stops in another file, or reveals a fixed value to a public result. Sema refuses only recursion (E0917), address-taking (E0918) and size (E0919). Nothing proves that zero marked calls remain.

log.text: All 4 criteria met; c1 proved on p233 (dev 22b864b785).

c1 is still open on dev 78f4541780. The evidence so far is IR Lint call.marked on ir.build (O0), ir.opt (O1/O2), CoreLibrary and eval.batch, plus the InlineContracts golden with inspect choices on O0/O1/O2. Missing: (1) a committed test that runs the zero-marked-Call census over Examples, Core and Compiler on each tier (the lint stops a build; no test counts); (2) the web path (calls from the JS partition into a marked #Export(wasm) function).

p206 (dev fe8c7b89ef): census-r3 dc38cfa29d (the call.marked IR lint, E1016/E1017, E0917 for cycles, guarantee text) and core-abs f9128ac736 landed. golden Contracts/InlineContracts passes; the suites show no new exit-101. Three ui snapshots fail: inline_always_scrub has a wrong fixture (ReadOnlyValueNotOwned fires before E1016), and cycle and reads_trace need their real spans blessed. Three O2 .err.out files cite shifted Math.jet lines. One fix SUB from PrecompiledCore-4; c1, c2 and c4 are met after it.

p205 (dev 16c1bda2d9): inspect-choices JSON line landed as 583f538540; cases build_entry/inspect_choices_shows_each_inlined_call_and_why passes. c1's census and golden, c2, c3 and c4 are queued for p206 (inline-always-refusals-census-r3 and core-abs-inline-always), with a full suite and self-build that must show zero new exit-101s.

p204 landed c1's first SUB (686cdaaee7), but its proof case inspect_choices_shows_each_inlined_call_and_why fails on the p204 batch compiler: 'JSON value differs: expected 7, got 4' on jet inspect choices -O2 --json. Sent back to PrecompiledCore-4 as its top priority.

criteria.text: Every direct call to an `#Inline(Always)` function is inlined on every tier: O0 (jet run, jet dev and compile-time code), O1, O2 and web where applicable. No build option removes a marked inline: `inline: off` and `--inline=off` cover only unmarked calls. Proof: a census after inlining on each tier counts zero Call ops whose callee is marked over Examples, Core and Compiler, run by a committed test; an example with golden output on O0/O1/O2 whose `jet inspect choices` lists every marked site as inlined.
criteria.evidence: p233 batch compiler (dev 22b864b785), commits 6bbd1eed99 (the inline_census suite) + cc69028f04: jet test Compiler --profile inline_census rc=0 PASS (Examples, Core and Compiler at O0/O1/O2 count zero Call ops to #Inline(Always) callees); jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Contracts/InlineContracts PASS on o0/o1/o2; jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter inspect_choices_shows_each_inlined_call_and_why PASS (jet inspect choices lists every marked site as inlined).

criteria.text: The inliner never quietly leaves a marked call: each reason it refuses a site today (a written parameter, a last-owner routine, a context.trace read, stops in another file, a fixed value revealed to a public result, and any other) is either handled by the inliner for marked callees or refused by sema with a registered diagnostic (what/why/fix and a UI snapshot), so a marked call that reaches codegen uninlined is an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a silent call. Proof: one UI snapshot per new diagnostic and one test per former refusal reason.
criteria.evidence: Landed c9a590769f (p213, dev 78f4541780). p213 batch compiler: jet test Compiler/JetIR/Source/OptInline.jet rc=0, with one test per former refusal reason (written parameter, last-owner routine, context.trace read, stops in another file, fixed value revealed to a public result, foreign body). The foreign body, the reason that was silently accepted, is now refused by sema as E1021 (registered, what/why/fix); ui --filter inline_always 7 passed, 0 bad, including the new inline_always_foreign snapshot. A marked call that reaches codegen uninlined stops the build through IR Lint call.marked (ICE). DiagnosticRows --check and DiagnosticCensus --check pass; the census is clean (jet check Core: no E1021 in Core).

criteria.text: Marked bodies cross module, package and precompiled-Core boundaries: a program that calls a Core or another package's `#Inline(Always)` function (for example core.math abs) gets the body inlined, with no call to it in the image on O0/O1/O2. Proof: `jet inspect choices` and an image symbol census for that program on each tier.
criteria.evidence: p206 batch compiler (dev fe8c7b89ef; core.math.abs marked #Inline(Always) in f9128ac736): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_entry/inline_always_crosses_package_and_core_boundaries → PASS 1 FAIL 0. The case calls abs, Int.abs() and a dependency package's marked gap across module, package and Core boundaries. It runs jet inspect choices on O0/O1/O2 and builds an image on each tier that holds neither core_math_abs nor geom_gap. The p206 suites show no new exit-101 (cases: the same 44 lines as p205).

criteria.text: The marker's reference text and its diagnostics say guarantee: the Markers spec and E0917-E0919 state that every direct call is inlined on every tier or the program is refused, with the full list of refusals. Proof: the spec text and the UI snapshots.
criteria.evidence: Landed c9a590769f (p213, dev 78f4541780). p213 batch compiler: the Markers reference text and every refusal (E0917-E0919, E1021) state the guarantee in their Why: every direct call is inlined on every tier or the program is refused, with the full list of refusals. ui --filter inline_always 7 passed, 0 bad (six re-blessed snapshots with the guarantee Why, plus E1021); cases inspect_choices_shows_each_inlined_call_and_why 1/0; golden InlineContracts passes in the p213 golden suite (0 FAIL).
